spec.slice:
S7b v3: the EXECUTOR half of the in-place resume, re-issued against HEAD 7a8e6cce (S6 hardening, the pause tombstone, the gated FoldWriter::seeded, the stage-1 no-fold-call rule, and the fold-RPC and ListToolActions Space-revocation checks are all committed). It covers:
- execution-core resume.rs: select_stage (infallible, downgrades only), in_place_scope, classify_claim, the pure restore, async restore_in_place, the unified args digest, and an ApprovedRelease that carries its class and action id.
- effect.rs: a ledger-read error that keeps the refusal class (denied / not persistent / other).
- fold.rs: save_fence.
- agent.rs:
  - prepare_resume split into consume_for_resume, released_call and build_segment;
  - ONE release pre-reserve before phase 2 in both stages, whatever the release's class and whether or not its slot passed phase 1;
  - RoundSeed::InPlace, the seeded writer and the pre_effect fence.
- closers.rs: the corrected decision table.
- EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED: mp-contracts, compose on execution-core and model-gateway, the contract rows, and the coupled-flip compose guard.
No proto change, no session-core change, no gateway or BFF change.
spec.summary:
This is the complete v3 design of S7b. I re-verified it with git show and the clean working tree at HEAD 7a8e6cce. The concurrent units v2 assumed are now committed, and I checked each assumption against the code:
- FoldWriter::seeded(channel, bearer, run_id, gate: WriterGate, expected_seq, segment_no) goes through WriterGate::decide.
- close_continued_pause is gone, and stage 1 makes no fold RPC.
- A content-refused pause fold is replaced by LoopFoldV1::tombstone, saved with kind `pause` under the pause's own pause_ref. session-core stores it as state `paused`, so it is claimable by pause_ref. It has extensions.not_resumable, pending None and an empty prompt_digest.
- The Space-revocation refusal on SaveLoopCheckpoint, ClaimLoopCheckpoint, CloseLoopCheckpoint and ListToolActions is PermissionDenied "Space membership required for this run".

Lead decisions applied:
- D1: there is NO attestation field. S7b adds no wire field and reads only committed fields.
  - The gateway pre-consume makes every executor consume a same-claim replay. The committed rule in prepare_resume (replay_is_fenced = effect::ledger_enabled()) accepts that replay only with the ledger on. This was verified, and so was the store side: orchestration_store::consume_approval hands the decrypted call back to a same-claim replay only, and answers NotFound once the run has ended.
  - The gateway resume switch, the executor resume switch, EXECUTION_EFFECT_LEDGER_ENABLED and SESSION_CORE_LOOP_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED are one coupled flip. A new compose guard requires each of them, plus AGENT_CONTINUE_AFTER_APPROVAL_ENABLED on both services, to be the plain `${NAME:-false}` interpolation of one shared variable.
  - The failure matrix spells out every mismatched flip.
- D2: the Space check stays after the consume, as defence in depth that cannot be reached today.
- D3: no close after a won claim.
- D6: the release is reserved through the ledger whatever its class, in both stages.
- D7: the already_terminal heartbeat reply and the expires_at gap are recorded as follow-ups.
- D8 and D9: the consume-to-fence windows are timed from the renewed recovery deadline, and continue_unreachable leaves the run to that window.

New relative to v2 (in amendments_to_prior_specs):
1. The release reserve moves out of phase 2 into ONE pre-reserve before phase 2, in both stages. It also runs when the release slot was rejected in phase 1 (that row is then finalized not_run). This closes a case v2 missed: a phase-1-rejected release was never reserved, so a second same-claim RunAgent could run a second model loop.
2. A PermissionDenied, Unauthenticated or ZDR-catalogue refusal from the ledger read refuses the continue instead of falling back to stage 1. effect::list_actions loses the status code at HEAD, so effect.rs gains LedgerReadError.
3. The claim table is corrected against loop_checkpoint::claim. "did not authenticate" is FailedPrecondition and check_fold is InvalidArgument (v2 had both under InvalidArgument). The ZDR trailer is read first. "loop checkpoint key unavailable" is a fallback.
4. The fingerprint cross-check is stated honestly. ConsumeApprovalResponse carries no fingerprint, so the pending-call identity rests on pause_ref, step_id, tool and args_digest. fold.pending.action_fingerprint must be non-empty, and it is compared only when the resume states one; the gateway states none.
5. PinnedRoute is unreachable as well: effective_authority refuses a pinned snapshot with authority_route_mismatch inside the consume step.
6. The contract guards are re-pointed. New guards check:
   - exactly one ConsumeApprovalRequest literal in execution-core, never with omit_call: true;
   - that save_fence( comes before reserve_release( in run_rounds;
   - the coupled-flip compose rule.

Build: 11 steps (0-10), each compiles and passes alone. No DB test is new or changed. Nothing in this spec has been written or run.
spec.approach:
VERIFIED STATE (HEAD 7a8e6cce, read with git show and the clean working tree; function names, not line numbers)

execution-core grpc.rs
- run_agent calls enforce_persistence_free_execution(&caller, req.zdr, "agent_run") before enforce_resume, so a ZDR caller or request is refused before any resume work.
- enforce_resume refuses failed_precondition "continue_disabled" when AGENT_CONTINUE_AFTER_APPROVAL_ENABLED is off.
- It refuses invalid_argument "resume_incomplete" unless mode is "segment" or "loop" and approval_id and claim_token are both set.

agent.rs run_agent_with_route
- Order: prepare_resume (the consume), apply_authority, tools and mode from the snapshot, heartbeat_managed_agent_run, no plan transition for a continuation, LoopContext{release, effect_ledger: effect::ledger_enabled(), step_prefix}, then run_rounds(ctx, goal, max_rounds, seeded_round).
- Every refusal before heartbeat_managed_agent_run therefore leaves the managed obligation untouched.

agent.rs prepare_resume
- It builds the ONLY Rust pb::ConsumeApprovalRequest literal in execution-core: 6 fields, no ..Default.
- replay_is_fenced = super::effect::ledger_enabled(). It proceeds iff `consumed.consumed || (consumed.already_consumed && consumed.same_claim && replay_is_fenced)`, otherwise failed_precondition "continuation_already_consumed".
- Then: approval_not_resumable, approval_snapshot_mismatch, approval_action_mismatch, effective_authority (authority_space_mismatch, then authority_route_mismatch, then authority_widened), step_prefix = s{next_segment_no(consumed.step_id)}., the call {id "approved"}, step id tool_step_id(prefix, 1, call) = s{N}.tool_1_approved, then not_releasable.

session-core orchestration_store::consume_approval
- CONSUME_APPROVAL_SQL wins once.
- A replay with consumed_at set and an equal claim hash returns already_consumed + same_claim WITH the decrypted call (read_consumed_call). Another claim gets no call.
- A cold ('') approval, a run that is not persistent, or a run that has ended answers NotFound, so a replay after recovery terminalized the run is refused.

agent.rs run_rounds
- One WriterGate literal: {switch: fold::checkpoint_enabled(), ledger: ctx.effect_ledger, zdr, waived: ctx.route.is_waived(), space: !req.space_id.is_empty(), depth: ctx.depth, resumed: ctx.release.is_some()}, with FoldWriter::new.
- fold_authority and fold_prompt_digest are computed only when the writer is engaged.
- The seeded_round is consumed by the first round, which skips inference.
- Phase 1 pre-pass:
  - checks, in order: truncation (stop_reason), allowlist, leaf role, rung, argument_problem (with grounding_conversation(messages)), main-agent-only, plan tool, plan mode, retrieval dedupe;
  - then step_seq += 1 and tool_step_id.
- retrievals_at_round_start is taken before phase 1.
- The pre_effect save runs only when effectful_calls > 0 (save_pre_effect, where Hold holds the effectful calls).
- Phase 2:
  - It builds a LedgerEntry only when `ctx.effect_ledger && class.is_effectful()`, and holds when `effects_held && ledger_entry.is_some()`.
  - AlreadyReserved gives closer UnknownOutcome, and sets released_step_replayed when ctx.release covers the call. After the batch, the request then ends Err failed_precondition "continuation_already_consumed".
  - A reserve Err gives a failed outcome "... could not be recorded ahead of time ... Try again."
  - finalize is best effort.

fold.rs
- FoldWriter::seeded(channel, bearer, run_id, gate: WriterGate, expected_seq, segment_no) goes through WriterGate::decide (OFF with the gate's reason; NoBearer). It is cfg_attr dead_code.
- SeqTracker::seeded and expected_seq exist.
- save_fold(kind, fold, pause_ref) is private.
- classify_status:
  - the ZDR trailer gives NotPersistent, read first;
  - Aborted loop_checkpoint_stale gives Stale;
  - loop_checkpoint_closed or loop_checkpoint_run_ended gives Closed;
  - loop_checkpoint_disabled gives StoreOff;
  - NotFound, PermissionDenied, Unauthenticated, Unimplemented and the key-unavailable message give Refused(..);
  - InvalidArgument or OutOfRange gives ContentRefused;
  - transport errors give Unavailable{ambiguous: true}.
- GATED_SAVE_TIMEOUT is 10 s.
- PauseFold::save on ContentRefused saves header.tombstone_bytes under kind `pause` and the pause's pause_ref.
- LoopFoldV1::tombstone has extensions.not_resumable, no messages, round_in_flight None, pending None and an empty prompt_digest. is_resumable() is false.
- The run_agent_with_route comment and the code confirm stage 1 makes no fold call; close_continued_pause and STAGE_ONE_CLOSE_REASON no longer exist (grep).

session-core grpc.rs claim_loop_checkpoint_inner and loop_checkpoint::claim
- Checks, in order:
  - authorize_operation "session:write";
  - refuse_zdr_continuation (DURABLE_MUTATION_FORBIDDEN, FailedPrecondition with the catalogue trailer);
  - the store switch (FailedPrecondition "loop_checkpoint_disabled");
  - authorize_run_owner(Mutate): NotFound "run not found", or PermissionDenied "Space membership required for this run" plus the ordinary owner refusals;
  - the cipher (FailedPrecondition "loop checkpoint key unavailable");
  - invalid_argument "claim token is required" (whitespace token);
  - run_owner_tx: NotFound, or DURABLE_MUTATION_FORBIDDEN for a non-persistent run;
  - FailedPrecondition "loop_checkpoint_run_ended".
- The CAS: state paused|parked, OR resuming with a lapsed lease, AND an equal pause_ref, becomes resuming with the claim hash and a lease of CLAIM_LEASE_SECONDS = 120. seq is NOT bumped.
- A miss is Aborted "loop_checkpoint_claim_held" (same token, same pause_ref, live lease), else FailedPrecondition "loop_checkpoint_not_claimable".
- After the CAS: FailedPrecondition "loop checkpoint did not authenticate", then check_fold InvalidArgument.
- CHECKPOINT_RESTORED is recorded in the claim transaction.
- The response is {seq, fold, segment_no, authority_digest, kind}.

session-core list_tool_actions_inner
- session:read, refuse_zdr_continuation, the store switch, authorize_run_owner(Read) (Space revocation PermissionDenied).

execution-core effect.rs
- list_actions returns Result<BTreeMap<String, LedgerRow>, String>, and the String is status.message(): the code is LOST.
- final_outcome_for("awaiting_approval") = "not_run".
- reserve sends effect_class = class.as_str().
- effect_class_of returns Read, Write or External only.

resume.rs
- The private args_digest (serde round trip) is used by ApprovedRelease. For JSON input it equals mp_contracts::effect_ledger::args_digest, assuming serde_json's preserve_order is not enabled (no Cargo.toml declares it; step 0 re-checks feature unification). For non-JSON input it differs, but consume refuses non-JSON (approval_not_resumable), so the swap is byte-identical.
- run_pause_mode returns '' for a Space or pinned run (one call site in run_rounds).
- resumed_step_id is #[allow(dead_code)].

closers.rs decide
- browser_agent first, then Keep only for has_output + Completed|Failed, then workspace, then Completed|Failed => ResultLost, then NotRun => Redispatch for every class, then Reserved|Unknown => an effect is UnknownOutcome and a read Redispatch, then None => Redispatch when ledger_was_on or the call is a read.

execution-core tests/durable_loop_contract.rs
- switch_table has 6 rows.
- fold_gate_violations: exactly one `WriterGate {` literal in agent.rs, carrying `waived: ctx.route.is_waived()` and zdr.
- builder_and_validator_violations: grpc.rs and agent.rs (non-test) never contain `.segment_no`.
- one_parser_violations for the continue env.

compose
- AGENT_CONTINUE_AFTER_APPROVAL_ENABLED: ${..:-false} on model-gateway and execution-core.
- EXECUTION_EFFECT_LEDGER_ENABLED and EXECUTION_LOOP_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED on execution-core.
- SESSION_CORE_LOOP_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED on session-core.
- There is NO EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED, LOOP_RESUME_ENV, loop_resume_enabled or omit_call anywhere.

agent.rs test MockSession
- claim_loop_checkpoint answers a fixed empty fold (claim_calls, claim_seq).
- list_tool_actions answers Unimplemented.
- consume_approval answers consume_response, or a won consume of delete_records.
- Recorder.order has save:/save_failed:/reserve/finalize/create_approval entries. consume and claim push nothing to order.

WIRE (D1): S7b adds no field. It reads or sends only these committed fields:
- AgentResume.{mode, approval_id, step_id, tool_name, action_fingerprint, brief, claim_token}. segment_no=8 is never read.
- ConsumeApprovalRequest 1-6 and ConsumeApprovalResponse 1-7 (ApprovedAuthority included).
- ClaimLoopCheckpointRequest 1-3 and ClaimLoopCheckpointResponse 1-5.
- SaveLoopCheckpointRequest as fold::save_rpc builds it.
- ListToolActionsRequest 1-2, ListToolActionsResponse.actions and ToolActionState 1-5 (closed_by=6 is not read).
- ReserveToolActionRequest 1-8 (args_digest=7, effect_class=8) and ReserveToolActionResponse.created.
- FinalizeToolActionRequest and HeartbeatManagedRunRequest.

The executor never sets ConsumeApprovalRequest.omit_call (D8, S7c field 7): it needs the descriptor. Once the lead's proto commit adds field 7, the hunk `omit_call: false` in consume_for_resume's literal lands in THAT commit (it is the only Rust literal, and it has no ..Default). The S7b guard forbids `omit_call: true` anywhere in execution-core, both before and after.

D1 IN THE EXECUTOR (what pre-consume means here)
- With the gateway's resume switch on, the gateway's ConsumeApproval (spend-only, which renews the managed obligation, D8) wins first. The executor's consume_for_resume is then a full same-claim replay: consumed=false, already_consumed=true, same_claim=true, and the decrypted call returned. The executor accepts it exactly by the committed rule, iff EXECUTION_EFFECT_LEDGER_ENABLED.
- The rule is unchanged and independent of the executor's resume switch, so a stage-1 continuation behind a pre-consume works whenever the ledger is on.
- A second /continue, with the same or another token, loses the gateway consume and gets 409 continuation_already_consumed before RunAgent. So the executor sees two same-claim RunAgents only from a non-gateway caller. The claim, the fence, the release pre-reserve and claim_held remain the fences for that case, and their refusals are marked unreachable through the gateway today.

A. STAGE SELECTION (pure, infallible, before any RPC)
resume::select_stage(mode, resume_on, checkpoint_on, ledger_on, zdr, waived) -> Stage:
- mode != "loop": Segment(None).
- Otherwise the first matching downgrade, in this order: ResumeSwitchOff, CheckpointOff, LedgerOff, Zdr, Waived. Each gives Segment(Some(d)) and one content-free info line "loop_resume_downgraded" {run_id, reason: d.as_str()}.
- Otherwise InPlace.
Notes:
- There is no refusal here. A switch-off or skewed `loop` is exactly `segment`, before and after the consume.
- zdr comes from req.zdr: defence in depth, since enforce_persistence_free_execution already refused it.
- waived comes from route.is_waived(). A waived consume is still refused by the S3 SQL (NotFound), so a waived run never claims, saves or continues.
- The inputs: resume_on = resume::loop_resume_enabled(), checkpoint_on = fold::checkpoint_enabled(), ledger_on = effect::ledger_enabled().

B. CONSUME
consume_for_resume(channel, bearer, &req, resume) -> Result<resume::Consumed, Status> is today's prepare_resume up to and including effective_authority, moved verbatim: the same literal, the same refusals and the same order.
- It adds one content-free warn line when `already_consumed && same_claim && !replay_is_fenced`: "continue_replay_refused_ledger_off" {run_id}. The status returned is unchanged.
- That line is the operator's signature of mismatch M1. It is the only change reachable with every switch off: a log line on a path that already refuses. No response differs.
- Consumed = {tool_name, tool_input_json, step_id, tools, mode, snapshot_authority, snapshot_digest, effective, segment: next_segment_no(step_id)}.
- released_call(&Consumed) -> (pb::ToolCall{id "approved"}, release_step_id = tool_step_id(s{N}., 1, call), ApprovedRelease).
- build_segment(Consumed, &req, resume) -> ResumedSegment is the rest of prepare_resume, unchanged (goal plus the framed brief, seeded_round, tools, mode, effective).

C. APPROVED RELEASE
- ApprovedRelease drops the private digest and uses mp_contracts::effect_ledger::args_digest: new() returns Err(Incomplete) when it is None, and covers() is false when the candidate's digest is None.
- It gains class: EffectClass = effect::effect_class_of(tool, input), computed in new(), plus accessors step_id(), tool_name(), class(), args_digest() and action_id() = effect::action_id_for(step_id).
- No other behaviour changes.

D. SCOPE (in place only; pure; after the consume, before the claim)
in_place_scope(&Consumed) -> Result<(), RestoreOrRefuse>:
- snapshot_authority.space_id non-empty gives Refuse(SpaceScopeUnsupported), failed_precondition "continue_space_scope_unsupported".
- provider_hint non-empty gives Fallback(PinnedRoute).
Both are unreachable today (D2):
- A Space or pinned run gets a '' approval from run_pause_mode, so continue_preflight answers not_resumable.
- If a request reached the executor anyway, effective_authority would already have refused authority_space_mismatch or authority_route_mismatch inside the consume step.
The check exists only so a future gateway that states the run's Space cannot restore a Space fold in place. The approval is then already spent (the consume committed).

E. CLAIM
restore_in_place sends ClaimLoopCheckpoint{run_id, pause_ref: format!("{}:{}", req.run_id, consumed.step_id), claim_token: resume.claim_token} under tokio timeout fold::GATED_SAVE_TIMEOUT, then classify_claim(&Status). The ZDR-catalogue trailer is checked FIRST, whatever the code.

| claim answer | effect |
|---|---|
| zdr_refusal::Refusal::from_status is Some | Refuse(DurableMutationForbidden): the catalogue status, as_str "durable_mutation_forbidden" |
| Aborted "loop_checkpoint_claim_held" | Refuse(ContinueInProgress), aborted "continue_in_progress"; unreachable through the gateway (D1) |
| FailedPrecondition "loop_checkpoint_run_ended" | Refuse(RunEnded), failed_precondition "not_resumable" |
| PermissionDenied or Unauthenticated (missing scope, not the owner, Space revocation) | Refuse(Forbidden), permission_denied "resume_forbidden" |
| FailedPrecondition "loop_checkpoint_not_claimable" | Fallback(FoldNotClaimable) |
| FailedPrecondition "loop_checkpoint_disabled" | Fallback(StoreDisabled) |
| FailedPrecondition "loop checkpoint did not authenticate", or InvalidArgument (check_fold, a whitespace token) | Fallback(FoldUnreadable) |
| FailedPrecondition "loop checkpoint key unavailable", or any other FailedPrecondition | Fallback(ClaimUnavailable) |
| NotFound, Unimplemented, Unavailable, DeadlineExceeded, Cancelled, Unknown, Internal, DataLoss, ResourceExhausted, a local timeout | Fallback(ClaimUnavailable) |

The answer is then parsed into ClaimedFold{seq, authority_digest, kind, segment: response segment_no, fold: LoopFoldV1::from_bytes}; a parse error is Fallback(FoldUnreadable).
- A claim that timed out may have committed. The row is then `resuming` under this token for at most 120 s; nothing closes it (D3), and stage 1 is fenced by the release pre-reserve.
- The ONLY reader allowed to restore a fold whose approval is consumed is this request: the holder of that consume's claim token, in the same RunAgent.

F. FOLD CHECKS (pure, in resume::restore, before the ledger read)
Each failure is a Fallback unless marked REFUSE.
1. kind == "pause" (park is S8): FoldKindMismatch.
2. fold.run_id == req.run_id: FoldRunMismatch.
3. claimed.segment == fold.segment_no: SegmentMismatch.
4. is_resumable(): NotResumable. This is the committed pause tombstone; it is checked before every content check.
5. extensions[effect_ledger] == true: LedgerOffInFold.
6. messages non-empty and messages[0].role == "system": HistoryInvalid.
7. fold.prompt_digest non-empty and equal to fold::prompt_digest_of(compose_system_prompt(snapshot tool names), snapshot tools): PromptDrift.
8. claimed.authority_digest == fold.authority.digest(): AuthorityDigestMismatch.
9. fold.authority.narrows(snapshot authority), else REFUSE AuthorityWidened.
10. fold.pending is Some, kind Approval, pause_ref == "{run_id}:{consumed.step_id}", step_id == consumed.step_id, call == consumed.tool_name, action_fingerprint non-empty and (resume.action_fingerprint empty OR equal): PendingMismatch.
11. round_in_flight is Some with 1..=64 calls, and exactly one call has step_id == consumed.step_id with name == consumed.tool_name, non-empty arguments_json, and effect_ledger::args_digest(fold args) == args_digest(consumed.tool_input_json), both Some: PendingMismatch.
12. Every completed entry maps to exactly one call (by step_id when non-empty, else by a unique call_id), and none maps to the pending call: RoundInvalid.
13. A call with an empty step_id has a completed entry: RoundInvalid. It is never dispatched.
14. rounds_executed >= 1 and step_seq >= 1: RoundInvalid.
15. consumed.segment == fold.segment_no + 1: SegmentMismatch.
16. (rounds_executed - 1) + delegated_rounds < effective.max_rounds (resolved), else BudgetSpent.

G. LEDGER CROSS-CHECK
One effect::list_actions read, under tokio timeout GATED_SAVE_TIMEOUT. The ids asked for are ledger_action_ids, the action_id_for of:
- (i) the release s{N}.tool_1_approved;
- (ii) the paused call's ORIGINAL step id;
- (iii) every other call with a non-empty step_id;
- (iv) resumed_step_id(N, s) for every call in (iii) with no completed entry (a dangling call).

Error mapping (new LedgerReadError, section J):
- Denied (PermissionDenied or Unauthenticated): REFUSE Forbidden.
- NotPersistent (ZDR trailer): REFUSE DurableMutationForbidden.
- A timeout or anything else: Fallback(LedgerUnavailable).
A PermissionDenied therefore never leads to a dispatch.

Rules:
- L1. Any row under (i): REFUSE ContinuationAlreadyConsumed. Every continuation of this approval, in either stage, pre-reserves (i) whenever the ledger is on (section I), so this catches an earlier attempt of any class, even one whose release was rejected in phase 1.
- L2. The paused step's row (ii):
  - absent or not_run: proceed;
  - completed or failed: REFUSE ContinuationAlreadyConsumed (a gated body cannot reach these: the Ask returns awaiting_approval before the body runs);
  - reserved or unknown_outcome (a failed best-effort finalize after the pause): Fallback(PausedStepUnsettled).
- L3. A (iii) row with another tool, or another digest when both are Some: Fallback(LedgerIdentityMismatch).
- L4. Dangling calls: section H.
- Absence is UNKNOWN, never not-run.
- What cannot be checked: actions of rounds after the paused one. They are structurally excluded: the claim matches only this approval's pause row, the paused round is the last round of the segment that wrote it, and any earlier continuation of this approval left an L1 row.

H. ROUND REBUILD (pure)
messages: the fold messages, as pb::ChatMessage.
response: pb::InferResponse{content: round_in_flight.assistant_content, tool_calls: the fold calls in order (the pending call keeps the fold's call id but takes consumed.tool_input_json as its arguments), stop_reason "tool_use"}.

Slots run parallel to the calls:
- A call with a completed entry becomes Resolved{name, output, error, passed_prepass: step_id non-empty}.
- The pending call becomes Release{step_id: the release id}.
- A dangling call is decided in this order:
  - G1, the withheld-argument rule, enforced here before closers::decide: an empty arguments_json gives Resolved with error closer_text(UnknownOutcome, name), whatever its class and its row. It is never Redispatch.
  - G2. A (iv) row exists and the call is effectful: Resolved closer_text(UnknownOutcome).
  - G3. Otherwise closers::decide(DanglingCall{class: the more effectful of effect_class_of(name, args) and the row's effect_class, ledger: the (iii) row status, has_output: false, workspace_available: false}). Close(kind) gives Resolved closer_text(kind). Redispatch gives Redispatch{step_id: resumed_step_id(N, original)}. Keep cannot occur, because has_output is false.

Counters:
- rounds_executed = fold - 1 (the loop's increment charges the open round once);
- delegated_rounds, step_seq, children_started, grounded and compaction_triggered as in the fold;
- attempted_retrievals = the fold's set (the round-start set for a pause fold);
- claimed_seq = claimed.seq; segment = N.
The field is named `segment`, so agent.rs never contains `.segment_no`.

I. ONE RELEASE PRE-RESERVE (both stages; ledger on only; D6)
In run_rounds, in the segment's FIRST round (the seeded one), after phase 1 and after the fence (in place), before phase 2, when ctx.effect_ledger and ctx.release is Some, call reserve_release(ctx, release):
- It sends effect::reserve with LedgerEntry{action_id: release.action_id(), tool: release.tool_name(), class: release.class() (read or none included), args_digest: release.args_digest()}.
- It runs whether or not the release slot passed phase 1. If the slot was rejected in phase 1 and the reserve is Created, it finalizes "not_run" at once.

| outcome | stage 1 | in place |
|---|---|---|
| Created | prereserved = Some(action_id) | prereserved = Some(action_id) |
| AlreadyReserved | Err failed_precondition "continuation_already_consumed" before phase 2 | Err failed_precondition "continuation_already_consumed" before phase 2 |
| Err | the release slot gets the committed failed outcome text ("... could not be recorded ahead of time, so it was held back. Try again."), it is not dispatched, and the loop continues exactly as today | Err Refusal::CheckpointUnavailable.status(): whether this attempt won the release is unknown, so nothing of the round is dispatched |

Stage 1 with AlreadyReserved is today's answer, now reached before any dispatch instead of after the batch, and for every class.

In phase 2:
- The LedgerEntry predicate becomes `ctx.effect_ledger && (class.is_effectful() || release covers (step_id, name, args))`, so the release slot keeps its entry for finalize.
- The reserve is skipped when entry.action_id == prereserved; it still finalizes.
- The hold keeps the effectful predicate: `effects_held && ledger_entry.is_some() && class.is_effectful()`.
- A non-release read is still never reserved. The released_step_replayed path stays for the AlreadyReserved answer of a non-prereserved release; it is unreachable once the pre-reserve exists, and is kept as defence in depth.

Behaviour change: only with ctx.release (the continue switch) and the ledger on. Every switch off is byte-identical.

J. LEDGER READ ERROR (effect.rs)
- pub(crate) struct LedgerReadError { kind: LedgerReadFailure::{Denied, NotPersistent, Other}, reason: String }.
- impl From<String> (Other), Display, and PartialEq<&str> comparing reason, so every existing list_actions test compiles and passes unchanged.
- list_actions_with maps a Status: the ZDR trailer gives NotPersistent; PermissionDenied or Unauthenticated give Denied; everything else is Other(status.message()).

K. LOOP WIRING
run_agent_with_route:
- select_stage, then consume_for_resume.
- Segment: build_segment.
- InPlace:
  - in_place_scope, then restore_in_place(&channel, bearer, &req, resume, &consumed, &release_step_id, &prompt_digest_of(compose_system_prompt(snapshot names), snapshot tools)).
  - A Fallback logs a content-free info "resume_fallback" {run_id, reason: token}, then build_segment with the SAME Consumed: no second consume, no close, no fold RPC.
  - A Refuse returns Err(status).
- Both stages:
  - apply_authority;
  - LoopContext.release = Some(release);
  - step_prefix = "s{N}.";
  - one content-free info line per continuation: "loop_resume_stage" {run_id, resume_stage: in_place | stage_one, fallback_reason: token or ""}.
- Every refusal from A-H returns before heartbeat_managed_agent_run. Refusals from the fence and the pre-reserve come after the run's first heartbeat, and they terminalize nothing.

run_rounds(ctx, goal, max_rounds, seed: Option<RoundSeed>), with enum RoundSeed { Segment(pb::InferResponse), InPlace(Box<resume::Restored>) }:
- in_place = matches!(seed, Some(RoundSeed::InPlace(_))).
- InPlace locals come from Restored. compose_system_prompt and fetch_skill_context are skipped, and the goal argument is never read.
- The ONE WriterGate literal gets `resumed: ctx.release.is_some() && !in_place`.
- The writer is FoldWriter::seeded(.., gate, restored.claimed_seq, restored.segment) for InPlace, else FoldWriter::new(.., gate).
- Phase 1 of the seeded in-place round walks the response calls with the seed slots:
  - A Resolved slot becomes CallSlot::Rejected(ToolStepResult{name, output, error}). It re-inserts its retrieval signature when passed_prepass, and makes no record_tool_step.
  - Release and Redispatch slots run every existing pre-pass gate. If they pass they take the seed slot's step id, with no step_seq increment (the fold's step_seq already counted them).
- FENCE (the seeded in-place round only, after phase 1, before the pre-reserve and phase 2):
  - folds.save_fence(the pre_effect fold built as the existing site builds it, from round_calls and fold_rejected; resolved slots carry an empty step_id and their outcome; the Release and Redispatch slots carry their new ids).
  - Any Err returns Refusal::CheckpointUnavailable.status().
  - The ordinary save_pre_effect is skipped for this round, so effects_held = false.
- Then the pre-reserve (I), then phases 2 and 3 unchanged.

L. LEASE, FENCING, ABANDONED CLAIM
- The 120 s lease covers the claim, the ledger read, the heartbeat and the fence: at most about 30 s worst case, bounded by three 10 s timeouts.
- Correctness does not rest on the lease:
  - Two claimants holding the same seq: one fence wins the compare-and-set and the other gets Stale, giving resume_checkpoint_unavailable.
  - A won fence makes the row `active`, so a later claimant gets not_claimable and falls back to stage 1.
  - The pre-reserve then lets exactly one attempt past.
- After the fence the row is never claimable, so a long release is safe.
- save_fence makes one RPC with no probe.
- D3: a fallback or refusal after a won claim never closes the fold. The row stays `resuming` for up to 120 s, then becomes claimable by pause_ref again; it is unusable:
  - the approval is consumed, so the gateway answers 409;
  - RunDetail.resumable is false (D5, S7c-A);
  - a same-claim replay that reached the executor would meet L1 once a release row exists.
  - The terminal purge removes it.
- A claimed tombstone costs one CHECKPOINT_RESTORED event and a 120 s `resuming` lease. This is accepted.

M. ZDR AND CREDENTIALS
- Nothing new is persisted except:
  - the fence fold, through the same writer, scrub, fit and gate;
  - a ledger row for a read, none or phase-1-rejected release, which holds ids, the class and a digest, never arguments.
- ZDR runs never reach the claim: the executor refuses the request first, select_stage downgrades, and the WriterGate is off.
- Waived runs downgrade before any claim, and their consume is refused by SQL.
- Logs carry run_id, stage, closed tokens and counts only.
- The claim token goes only to session-core, and no bearer or token is put in a fold.

"2026-10-18, S7b v3 in-place resume rules (WS03).
(0) No attestation field. A gateway pre-consume makes the executor's consume a same-claim replay, which the executor accepts only with EXECUTION_EFFECT_LEDGER_ENABLED. The gateway resume switch, the executor resume switch, the ledger and the session-core fold store are one coupled flip, pinned in compose by the durable_loop_contract coupled-flip guard.
(1) The switch is EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED (default false, strict `true`). With it off, a prerequisite off, or a ZDR or waived run, `loop` runs as `segment`: a downgrade, never a refusal.
(2) Order: consume (with effective_authority), the scope check, claim by `{run_id}:{consumed step}`, fold checks, one ledger read, restore, apply_authority, a pre_effect fence at the claimed seq, the release pre-reserve, then dispatch. A failed fence or a failed pre-reserve in place is resume_checkpoint_unavailable, with nothing dispatched.
(3) One release action per approval, `s{N}.tool_1_approved`, pre-reserved in both stages whatever its class, and even when its slot is rejected in phase 1. A second attempt ends continuation_already_consumed before any dispatch.
(4) A restore failure falls back to stage 1 under the same consume and never closes the fold.
(5) Absence is unknown. A recorded output wins. Withheld arguments are never redispatched. A paused step that completed or failed refuses; one left reserved or unknown_outcome falls back.
(6) A PermissionDenied, Unauthenticated or ZDR refusal from the claim or the ledger read refuses, and is never a fallback.
(7) continue_space_scope_unsupported is checked on the consumed snapshot; it is defence in depth while the gateway states no Space."

risks: Coupled flip (D1). Every executor consume behind the S7c pre-consume is a same-claim replay. With EXECUTION_EFFECT_LEDGER_ENABLED off at the executor, it is refused continuation_already_consumed AFTER the gateway spent the click. The compose guard pins the wiring, not a live deployment: an operator who overrides one service's variable can still mismatch. Detection: the warn line continue_replay_refused_ledger_off plus the gateway's approval_spent frame.

Stage-1 behaviour change (step 7, ledger and continue switch on):
- Every release, read, none and phase-1-rejected included, writes a ledger row and adds one reserve (plus a finalize) before phase 2.
- A failed pre-reserve holds the release with today's text.
- AlreadyReserved now ends the request before dispatch, where it used to end it after the batch.
With every switch off, behaviour is byte-identical.

Stale active fold. An in-place attempt that wins the fence and loses the pre-reserve leaves an `active` fold it never acts on. It is purged at terminalization. S8 must never recover an active fold whose approval is consumed or whose release row belongs to another attempt.

A fence or pre-reserve failure after a won consume strands the approval (409 thereafter). The run is left to the recovery window renewed at the gateway consume and by the executor heartbeat. This is an accepted consequence of failing closed (D9).

The heartbeat's already_terminal reply is still ignored (D7 follow-up). A run that recovery terminalized between the gateway consume and the executor start would have its replay refused NotFound by the store, so nothing is dispatched. A run that terminalized after the claim keeps going until its next fold save gets loop_checkpoint_run_ended (writer Failed, effects held).
The Space check and PinnedRoute are unreachable today (D2). If the gateway ever states the run's Space, the refusal comes after the consume and spends the click.
L2 relies on the Ask gate returning before the tool body runs (true of execute_step_with_subagent today). A future gate that runs part of a body before asking needs L2 revisited.

An abandoned claim leaves a `resuming` fold and one CHECKPOINT_RESTORED event for a restore that did not continue; a claimed tombstone does too. Both are accepted (D3). RunDetail.resumable must exclude the consumed approval (D5, S7c-A).
Byte identity of the rebuilt history holds only modulo the scrub_fold redactions and the fit() compaction applied at save time.

The pending-call identity rests on pause_ref, step_id, tool and args digest. ConsumeApprovalResponse carries no fingerprint, so the fold's fingerprint is compared only against a stated resume fingerprint, and the gateway states none.
workspace_available is always false, so a dangling workspace tool is always closed. This is conservative.
Prompt drift after a deploy sends every in-flight pause to stage 1. This is safe.
classify_claim and the ledger-read mapping turn a PermissionDenied from a proxy misconfiguration or a missing scope into resume_forbidden. They fail closed, and the click is spent.
agent.rs is large and hot. Steps 6-9 must be serialized with any other unit that touches run_rounds (reconcile: strictly sequential editors of agent.rs).
invariants: ConsumeApproval stays the only authority gate. The claim, the fence, the release pre-reserve and the shared release id are second-line guards.
Order: select_stage, consume (with effective_authority), in_place_scope, claim, fold checks, ledger read, restore, apply_authority, heartbeat, fence, release pre-reserve, dispatch.

No call of the resumed round reaches a reserve or a dispatch before a pre_effect fold is saved at the claimed seq. No call of either stage's first round is dispatched before this attempt has reserved the release action (ledger on).

One step id and one ledger action per approval, s{N}.tool_1_approved. It is pre-reserved whatever its class and whether or not phase 1 accepted it, whenever the ledger is on. At most one model loop continues an approval among executor requests that share its claim.
The executor accepts a same-claim consume replay only with the ledger on (committed rule, unchanged). There is no attestation field and no new wire field.
The released call's name and arguments come from the consumed descriptor, never from the fold, and every pending-call digest is mp_contracts::effect_ledger::args_digest.

A call with an empty step_id or withheld arguments is never dispatched by a resume. A recorded output wins. An effect that is absent, reserved or unknown is never re-run. Absence from ListToolActions is unknown.
A paused step whose row completed or failed refuses the continue. A paused step left reserved or unknown_outcome falls back. The paused step is never dispatched under its own id.

A tombstone is claimable but never restored. Only the request holding the consume's claim token restores a consumed approval's fold, and a fold whose approval is consumed is never offered to anyone else.
A fallback reuses the Consumed value, makes no fold RPC and does not close the fold (D3).
A PermissionDenied, Unauthenticated or ZDR-catalogue answer from the claim, the ledger read or the fence ends the request with nothing dispatched.

select_stage never refuses. With EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED or any prerequisite off, or for a ZDR or waived run, `loop` is exactly `segment`. With every switch off, runtime behaviour is byte-identical to HEAD, apart from one content-free warn line on an already-refusing path.
Only a persistent, non-Space, unpinned, non-waived depth-0 run reads a fold. The one WriterGate literal decides the writer, for both new and seeded.
No executor refusal terminalizes the run. Every A-H refusal precedes the first heartbeat.
Nothing is persisted beyond the gated, scrubbed folds and argument-free ledger rows. Logs are content-free. No bearer or claim token is logged or put in a fold.
The executor never reads AgentResume.segment_no and never sets ConsumeApprovalRequest.omit_call to true.

I verified that orchestration_store::consume_approval returns the decrypted call to a same-claim replay only, and answers NotFound once the run has ended. s7c-v2's 'replay_ok = resume.consumed_by_gateway || ledger' and its fallback wording are superseded by the coupled flip and the new coupled_flip_violations compose guard.

failure_matrix: F1. Space or pinned run, today's gateway. User sees: 409 not_resumable at the gateway (the approval is cold). Hypothetically, at the executor: authority_space_mismatch or authority_route_mismatch after the consume. Safe: nothing claimed or run. Future shape (the gateway states a Space): continue_space_scope_unsupported after the consume, before the claim, and the click is spent.

W1 (consume-to-fence). The gateway pre-consume committed, then the gateway died before RunAgent. User sees: the stream drops; a retry gets 409 continuation_already_consumed. Safe: nothing ran. The fold stays paused and is never offered (resumable false, D5). Recovery terminalizes about 15 min after the consume (D8 renewal), and the purge removes the fold.

W2. RunAgent connect refused after a won pre-consume (continue_unreachable). User sees: a typed non-retryable frame with approval_spent. Safe: nothing ran. The run is left to the renewed window and is not terminalized at once (D9).

W3. The executor replay consume was answered, then the executor crashed before the claim. User sees: a dropped stream or an unknown-outcome frame, then 409. Safe: nothing claimed or run. The run is recovered after the renewed window.
W4. The executor's replay meets a run that recovery already ended. User sees: NotFound from the store, relayed as a refusal frame. Safe: the store withholds the call; nothing ran.

F2. The consume or replay is refused (not granted, expired, not resumable, snapshot or action mismatch, not_releasable, authority_*). User sees: the existing closed tokens. Safe: no claim, no heartbeat; the fold is still paused.
F3. A crash after the consume, before the claim (switch-off path, executor-owned consume). User sees: the stream drops, then 409. Safe: nothing ran.

F5. The claim is held by the same token. User sees: continue_in_progress (stream only). This is unreachable through the gateway (D1: a second request gets 409 first). Safe: the first holder owns the run.

F6. The claim answers not_claimable, disabled, unreadable, key unavailable, not found, unimplemented, transport or timeout. User sees: a stage-1 continuation. Safe: one consume and no fold RPC; the release is pre-reserved whatever its class.
F7. run_ended. User sees: not_resumable. Safe: nothing run.
F8. The ZDR trailer on the claim or the ledger read. User sees: the catalogue refusal. Safe: no fold restored, nothing dispatched.
F9. PermissionDenied or Unauthenticated on the claim or the ledger read (Space revocation, scope, owner). User sees: resume_forbidden. Safe: nothing dispatched, not even stage 1.

F10. A crash after the claim, before the fence. User sees: the stream drops, then 409. Safe: the fold is resuming for at most 120 s and then unusable (consumed approval). The executor heartbeat (if it was reached) or the gateway renewal sets the recovery window.

F11. A restore check fails (tombstone, kind, segment, drift, ledger off in the fold, history, authority digest, pending or round mismatch, budget). User sees: stage 1. Safe: same consume, no close, no fold RPC; the release is pre-reserved.
F12. The fold authority is wider than the snapshot's. User sees: authority_widened. Safe: nothing dispatched.
F13. The ledger read times out or errors. User sees: stage 1. Safe: the release pre-reserve fences it.
F14a. L1: a release row exists. User sees: continuation_already_consumed. Safe: no second continuation.
F14b. L2: the paused step's row is completed or failed. User sees: continuation_already_consumed. Safe: the approved effect is not repeated.
F14c. L2: the paused step's row is reserved or unknown_outcome (a failed finalize). User sees: stage 1. Safe: the gated body never ran; the release runs once under its own id.
F15. L3: the ledger tool or digest disagrees. User sees: stage 1.
F15b. A dangling call has withheld arguments, or an absent or unknown effect. User sees: the model is told the outcome is unknown. Safe: never redispatched.
F16. The seeded writer's gate says off (NoBearer). User sees: resume_checkpoint_unavailable. Safe: no dispatch.
F17. The fence answers Stale (another claimant won the seq). User sees: resume_checkpoint_unavailable. Safe: only the winner dispatches.
F18. The fence is unavailable, timed out, closed, run_ended, denied or content-refused. User sees: resume_checkpoint_unavailable. Safe: nothing dispatched and nothing reserved.

F19. A crash after the fence, before the pre-reserve. User sees: the stream drops, then 409. Safe: no release row. The active fold is never claimable; S8 must not recover it without an owner check. Recovery after the deadline.

F20. The pre-reserve answers AlreadyReserved (another attempt in either stage won). User sees: continuation_already_consumed. Safe: this attempt dispatched nothing. A stale active fold (in place) is left to the purge.

F21. The pre-reserve errors. In place: resume_checkpoint_unavailable, nothing dispatched. Stage 1: the release gets today's held-back text and the loop continues (the model replans), with the release not run.

F22. A crash between the pre-reserve and the dispatch, or during the dispatch. User sees: the stream drops. Safe: the row is reserved, and the sweep makes it unknown_outcome; it is never retried as an effect. A later attempt meets L1.
F23. A crash after the release completed, before the round fold. User sees: the stream drops. Safe: the row is completed; a later recovery gives ResultLost.

F24. A slow resume: claim to fence takes more than 120 s and a duplicate claims (non-gateway caller only). User sees: one proceeds; the other gets resume_checkpoint_unavailable or continuation_already_consumed. Safe: the CAS fence and the pre-reserve.
F25. A released call longer than 120 s. User sees: a normal continuation. Safe: the row is active and not claimable.

F27. A same-claim replay with a read, consent-gated or phase-1-rejected release, in either stage. User sees: the second request ends continuation_already_consumed. Safe: one model loop; later-round effects are not re-issued.
F28. The resumed segment pauses again. User sees: a new loop-mode approval. Safe: segment N, the s{N}. prefix, the chained seq and pause_ref {run}:{s{N}.step}.

M1 (coupled-flip mismatch). Gateway resume on, executor EXECUTION_EFFECT_LEDGER_ENABLED off. The executor refuses the same-claim replay with continuation_already_consumed after the gateway spent the click. User sees: a typed non-retryable frame with approval_spent on EVERY continue, and the click is lost. The run is left to the renewed recovery window. Operator signature: the executor warn line continue_replay_refused_ledger_off on each attempt, with zero claims. Fix: turn the ledger on (and EXECUTION_LOOP_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED) or the gateway switch off.

M2. Gateway resume on, executor EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED off, ledger on. The executor downgrades `loop` to stage 1 and accepts the replay. User sees: a normal stage-1 continuation. Operator signature: loop_resume_downgraded reason=resume_switch_off. Safe.

M3. Gateway on, executor EXECUTION_LOOP_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED off. No pause folds are written, so RunDetail.resumable is false and the gateway sends `segment`; with the ledger on, stage 1 works. If a stale `loop` arrives: downgraded checkpoint_off. Safe.

M4. Gateway on, SESSION_CORE_LOOP_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED off. resumable is false, so `segment`; the executor's writer goes off on loop_checkpoint_disabled; a stray claim answers disabled, giving Fallback(StoreDisabled). User sees: stage 1. Safe with the ledger on.

M5. Gateway resume off, executor on. No pre-consume, and the committed continue_resume sends mode `segment`, so the executor runs today's stage 1 with its own winning consume. User sees: today's behaviour. Safe.

M6. Deploy order violated: gateway on, executor image still pre-S7b. The old executor accepts `loop` (enforce_resume) and runs stage 1, accepting the replay iff its ledger is on. A read release is not pre-reserved there, so the read-release double-loop guard is absent until the executor is upgraded; it is reachable only by a non-gateway same-claim caller.

M7. Gateway resume on, executor AGENT_CONTINUE_AFTER_APPROVAL_ENABLED off. enforce_resume answers continue_disabled AFTER the gateway pre-consume. User sees: a typed frame with approval_spent, and the click is lost. Operator signature: continue_disabled right after a won pre-consume. The compose guard requires both services to interpolate the same variable.

M8. Session-core older than S7c-A (no omit_call or renewal) behind a new gateway: S7c's concern. For the executor nothing changes: its replay is a full consume either way. The recovery window is then the executor's first heartbeat, not the consume.

findings.issue: The closers decision table in the design contradicts itself on a recorded browser output. That leaves the required test assertions undefined and breaks the 'a recorded output wins' invariant.
findings.evidence: file_changes lists rule 1 as 'has_output => Keep, whatever the ledger says' and rule 2 as 'browser_agent => Close(NotResumableTool)'. The same entry then says 'put the browser rule FIRST when has_output is false; rule 1 applies only to non-browser tools'. amendments_to_prior_specs says rule 1 'applies after the browser_agent rule'. The invariants say 'A recorded output wins'. The binding requirement is has_output + Reserved/None => Keep. At HEAD decide() checks browser_agent first, then Keep only for has_output + Completed|Failed. Under the last reading, has_output + browser_agent closes as NotResumableTool and discards a known result. restore always passes has_output=false, so this is dead until S8, but the unit test a_browser_run_is_never_resumed gains a 'has_output variant' with no stated expected value.
findings.suggested_fix: State one order in one place. Recommended: has_output => Keep for every tool, because Keep never re-runs anything. Then browser_agent without output => Close(NotResumableTool). Then workspace, ResultLost, NotRun, Reserved|Unknown, None. Give the exact expected value of the new has_output + browser_agent test, and drop the contradictory sentences.

findings.issue: reserve_release is specified with a LedgerEntry of only {action_id, tool, class, args_digest}. It omits run_id, data_category and zdr. session-core binds a reservation's identity to all of them, so a mismatch reopens the second-model-loop hole the pre-reserve is meant to close.
findings.evidence: effect::LedgerEntry has run_id, action_id, tool, data_category, zdr, class and args_digest. Phase 2 builds it with data_category(&call.name) and zdr. reserve_tool_action_inner compares (request_id, tool, data_category, zdr, args_digest, effect_class) against the existing row and returns Status::already_exists('tool action identity is bound to different immutable input') on any difference. effect::reserve flattens every Err to status.message(). The design's stage-1 table sends Err to 'held back, loop continues exactly as today'. If the pre-reserve entry differs from the phase-2 entry, or from a row an earlier HEAD attempt wrote, a same-claim replay gets Err instead of created=false. It then continues a model loop beside the first, which is the INV-02 case.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the release's LedgerEntry through the same constructor as the phase-2 entry (same data_category(&name), zdr, run_id, class, effect::args_digest_of). Add a test that the pre-reserve and phase-2 entries are field-for-field equal. State in the spec that an already_exists identity conflict is treated as AlreadyReserved, or that it refuses, in stage 1.

findings.issue: The fence fold is built 'as the existing site builds it', which writes an empty step_id for every Resolved slot. Sibling calls that actually ran are therefore recorded as refused-before-dispatch. S8 will read this fold when it recovers a crashed in-place run.
findings.evidence: At HEAD round_calls maps CallSlot::Rejected to an empty step id. The design turns every completed sibling into CallSlot::Rejected(ToolStepResult). The loop_fold.rs RoundInFlight contract says 'A call rejected before dispatch has an empty step_id' and 'a call whose step_id is empty was refused, never dispatched'. The design also re-inserts a retrieval signature only 'when passed_prepass', which is step_id non-empty. A later resume from the fence fold sees empty step ids, so it cannot re-insert those signatures. It would then admit a duplicate knowledge_search that the original round suppressed. It also loses the ledger key for effects that ran.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the original step id on SeedSlot::Resolved and use it in the fence's round_calls. Their completed entries keep step_id and call_id, and the Release and Redispatch slots carry their new ids. Add a test that the fence fold's calls keep the original step ids of the siblings that ran.

findings.issue: Coupled-flip hazard M1 is catastrophic and can be triggered by one routine operator action. The compose guard pins wiring only, not coupling. The 'one shared variable' wording is also inaccurate.
findings.evidence: The gateway pre-consume has no view of the executor's EXECUTION_EFFECT_LEDGER_ENABLED. Turning the ledger off alone, a plausible rollback of a safety feature, makes the executor refuse every same-claim replay (replay_is_fenced=false) after the gateway has spent the click. Every /continue then loses its click and the run is stranded for about 15 minutes (M1). The seven guarded keys are different variables, so no single operator variable flips them together. coupled_flip_violations reads only docker-compose.yml. The other compose files (override, production, release, bridges) are scanned only by every_switch_defaults_off_violations, so a literal override in one of them decouples the flip unseen. AGENT_CONTINUE_AFTER_APPROVAL_ENABLED uses the lenient parser (1/on/yes) while the other switches use switch_from (strict 'true'). A value of '1' therefore flips continue on and leaves the strict switches off.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not reopen D1. Keep the guard but extend coupled_flip_violations to the sibling compose files and reword the 'one variable' claim. Add an executor startup warning and a counter for EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED=true with the ledger or checkpoint off. Add the strict-versus-lenient parser trap to the operator note and the failure matrix. Record the S7c option of passing the ledger variable to model-gateway so loop_resume_enabled() there is conjunctive.

findings.issue: The binding rule 'cross-check the ledger against the fold and fall back when the ledger holds actions the fold does not account for' is met only for ids derivable from the fold. The deviation is not recorded as one. L2 also consults the paused step's original row, which the reconcile text says is 'never consulted'.
findings.evidence: ListToolActions needs named ids, so ledger_action_ids covers only items (i)-(iv). The design's 'What cannot be checked' argues that later-round rows are structurally excluded, because every earlier continuation of this approval leaves an L1 row. That argument fails for a same-claim attempt by a pre-S7b executor image. The old image never reserved a read release, and its stage 1 never touches the fold. The fold would then still be claimable with no L1 row. M6 only mentions the double-loop guard, not this. No test covers a ledger row for a later-round action. reconcile.json says 'NotRun on the ORIGINAL paused step is never consulted'. L2 consults it for refuse and fallback, although it never feeds closers::decide.
findings.suggested_fix: Record both points as explicit deviations in the ledger text. State that the structural exclusion depends on the executor image deploying first (D10). Add a restore test that documents the limit. Reword the reconcile bullet to 'never fed to closers::decide'.

findings.issue: The completed-entry matching rule is underspecified for calls whose provider id is empty. Such pauses always fall back to stage 1.
findings.evidence: check 12 matches 'by step_id when non-empty, else by a unique call_id'. fold_completed writes call_id: call.id.clone(), and FoldCompleted skips an empty call_id when serializing. tool_step_id already handles an empty call id by using the tool name, so empty ids are a real input. With an empty-id rejected call, or two of them, matching is ambiguous and the result is RoundInvalid.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a positional fallback. Completed entries are written in call order, excluding the paused call, so they can be matched by position when call_id is empty. Or state that this falls back, and add a test that fixes the behaviour.

findings.issue: The in-place fence path is not specified for a writer that is not Active, where fold_authority is None.
findings.evidence: fold_authority and fold_prompt_digest are built only when folds.engaged(). The fence needs both to build its fold. F16 states the outcome (resume_checkpoint_unavailable) but not the code path when fold_authority.as_ref() is None. Separately, Section K says refusals from the fence and the pre-reserve come after 'the run's first heartbeat'. In fact there are two heartbeats before the seeded round: heartbeat_managed_agent_run in run_agent_with_route and the one at the top of run_rounds.
findings.suggested_fix: State that the seeded in-place round returns CheckpointUnavailable before building any fold when the writer is not Active or fold_authority is None. Test it with an Off writer. Fix the heartbeat wording.

findings.issue: The design says no DB test is new. The central in-place fencing argument (save at the claimed seq on a resuming row; same-seq reclaim after a lapsed lease with exactly one fence winning) is pinned by no existing session-core DB test.
findings.evidence: Existing #[ignore] tests: one_claim_wins_a_pause_and_the_fold_opens_under_its_scope, loop_checkpoint_claim_held_is_told_apart_from_losing_the_pause, and a_rejoin_restores_the_save_claim_and_close_of_a_fold, which saves a round at the claimed seq. None claims, lets the lease lapse, reclaims with another token, and then races two saves at the same seq. save() checks only seq and closed, so the behaviour follows from the code, but nothing guards it. redteam INV-09 expected an Aborted for the first holder, which HEAD does not give.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test-only #[ignore] DB test for the lead's harness. It does pause, claim A, lapse the lease, claim B, then fence A (ok, row active, claim cleared), then fence B (stale), then a claim of the row (not_claimable). Name it in the verification notes.

findings.issue: Step 9 bundles the run_agent_with_route wiring, the run_rounds in-place initialization, the seeded writer, the phase-1 seed hooks, the fence, the MockSession knobs, about 25 new tests, the removal of every dead_code allow and nine mutation checks into one step. It has no intermediate green state if a part has to be backed out.
findings.evidence: The steps list reads: step 9 wiring, with the sub-bullets run_agent_with_route, run_rounds InPlace init, the seeded writer, phase-1 hooks, save_fence, the pre-reserve error mapping, MockSession knobs and agent tests, the dead_code removals, and the mutation checks. agent.rs is the large hot file that the reconcile rules say must have strictly sequential editors.
findings.suggested_fix: Split step 9. 9a wires select_stage, consume, in_place_scope and restore_in_place, with every Fallback and Refuse path, building the Restored value but running stage 1 regardless. 9b adds the RoundSeed::InPlace initialization, the seeded writer and the phase-1 hooks. 9c adds the fence and the in-place pre-reserve mapping, then removes the dead_code allows. Run the mutation checks after 9c.

checked: Verified at HEAD 7a8e6cce: prepare_resume order, its single ConsumeApprovalRequest literal and the replay_is_fenced rule. Also verified that only agent.rs production code holds that literal, and that omit_call and EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED are absent everywhere.

Verified in session-core: consume_approval replays hand the decrypted call to the same claim only, and answer NotFound once the run has ended. The replay branch runs before the expiry check. The consume SQL joins runs and requires persistent retention.

Verified claim(): paused or parked, or a lapsed resuming row, matched by pause_ref. seq is not bumped. The error classes and their order match the design's classify_claim table. save() compares only seq and closed, so a fence at the claimed seq succeeds, sets the row active and clears the claim. A second claimant at the same seq gets stale. An existing DB test already saves a round at the claimed seq after a claim.

Verified the pause fold: pause_ref is {run_id}:{step_id}, pending carries the descriptor fingerprint, it is saved before CreateApproval, and the paused round's completed entries cover every call except the pending one. Dangling calls therefore cannot occur in a pause fold. Walked G1-G3 and the fence over the pre_effect and park kinds.

Verified run_rounds: single WriterGate literal, retrievals_at_round_start before the pre-pass, effects_held and save_pre_effect, the phase-2 ledger predicate, AlreadyReserved with released_step_replayed, reserve Err text, and phase-3 pause fold construction. Child contexts carry release None. The loop top heartbeats before the seeded round. Segment numbering (first writer segment 1, next_segment_no 2, check 15) is consistent.

Verified fold.rs: FoldWriter::seeded takes the gate, SeqTracker::seeded, classify_status, GATED_SAVE_TIMEOUT 10 s, the pause tombstone, and is_resumable. Verified closers.rs, effect.rs, resume.rs, the ApprovedRelease::new callers and existing tests. A PartialEq<&str> LedgerReadError keeps the existing effect tests compiling.

Walked adjacent-step kill points in the in-place and stage-1 flows: gateway consume, executor consume, claim, ledger read, heartbeat, fence, pre-reserve, dispatch, finalize and the round fold. No path duplicates an effect, and none strands a run beyond the accepted D9 recovery window. Also walked two same-claim attempts racing across the fence and the pre-reserve. Walked the mismatched flips (ledger off, resume off, checkpoint off, session-core off, old executor image, Unimplemented RPCs). The failure matrix is complete for them.

Checked the lead decisions against the design: D1 (no attestation field), D2, D3 (no close after a won claim), D6, D7, D8/D9, D10 and D11 are applied or left open as instructed. Checked the contract-test claims: switch_table, fold_gate_violations, the .segment_no guard, the one-parser guard, and the compose lines for all seven coupled keys. Checked the ZDR and waived gates: persistence-free refusal before enforce_resume, the SQL and run_owner_tx retention checks, and the gateway stating no Space or route. No new content-persisting boundary was found beyond the gated fence fold and argument-free ledger rows.

findings.issue: In stage 1 the release pre-reserve treats every Err the same way: the release gets the 'held back, Try again' text and the model loop continues. Two cases make the stated guard false. (a) A reserve that timed out after it committed. (b) An ALREADY_EXISTS answer. session-core reserve_tool_action_inner returns already_exists('tool action identity is bound to different immutable input') when request_id, tool, data_category, zdr, args_digest or effect_class differ from the stored row, and effect::reserve maps that to Err, not AlreadyReserved. In both cases a second same-claim attempt can also continue, so two model loops run beside each other. The invariant 'At most one model loop continues an approval among executor requests that share its claim', and F27, overclaim. Section I's LedgerEntry also names only {action_id, tool, class, args_digest}. It leaves out data_category and zdr, which the identity binding compares against the phase-2 / pre-S7b executor row (M6).
findings.evidence: effect.rs reserve(): `.map_err(|status| status.message().to_owned())`, so the code is lost. grpc.rs reserve_tool_action_inner: `existing.2 != req.data_category || existing.3 != req.zdr || ... => Status::already_exists(...)`. The agent.rs phase-2 LedgerEntry uses `data_category: data_category(&call.name), zdr`. The design, section I, Err row for stage 1: 'the loop continues exactly as today'.
findings.suggested_fix: Make reserve_release (or effect::reserve) map ALREADY_EXISTS to AlreadyReserved, so a stage-1 continuation ends with continuation_already_consumed. State that the pre-reserve LedgerEntry uses data_category(release.tool_name()) and req.zdr, exactly as phase 2 does. Either refuse in stage 1 on an ambiguous (transport or timeout) reserve error, or weaken the invariant and F27 to say 'unless the release pre-reserve errored', and list it as a risk reachable only by a non-gateway same-claim caller.

findings.issue: The new coupled_flip_violations guard adds nothing that compose_violations does not already check. compose_violations already requires every switch_table row to be exactly `${KEY:-false}` on its service, which also covers the 'a :-true default' and 'removed execution-core ledger row' mutations. The guard also cannot express the D1 coupling. EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED, EXECUTION_EFFECT_LEDGER_ENABLED, EXECUTION_LOOP_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED and SESSION_CORE_LOOP_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED are four separately named operator variables, so the summary's 'the plain ${NAME:-false} interpolation of one shared variable' is true only per name. Setting EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED=true without the ledger (M1, clicks lost on every continue) passes every guard.
findings.evidence: compose_violations: `let want = format!("${{{key}:-false}}")` for each (service, key) in switch_table. switch_table already lists execution-core ledger, checkpoint and continue, model-gateway continue, session-core checkpoint and sweep. The design: 'Each of these must be exactly `${NAME:-false}`, interpolating the variable of its own name, so one operator variable flips both services'.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the two new switch_table rows and drop the duplicate guard, or reword it honestly as a per-name pin. Add a real detector for D1 mismatches: an execution-core startup check that logs one loud content-free error line when loop_resume_enabled() is on and effect::ledger_enabled(), fold::checkpoint_enabled() or continue_enabled() is off. With the shared EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED name, the executor sees the same value as the gateway, so this catches M1 and M7 at boot, before a click is spent. Then state precisely in the risks what compose can and cannot pin.

findings.issue: The new decision table contradicts itself. The numbered list puts '1. has_output => Keep, whatever the ledger says' before '2. browser_agent'. The same entry then says 'put the browser rule FIRST when has_output is false; rule 1 applies only to non-browser tools', and the amendments say rule 1 applies AFTER the browser rule. An implementer following the numbered list would turn a recorded browser output into Keep, which breaks the intended has_output variant of a_browser_run_is_never_resumed. The phrase 'browser first when has_output is false' is also wrong, because browser comes first regardless of has_output.
findings.evidence: The committed decide(): `if call.tool_name == NOT_RESUMABLE_TOOL { return Close(NotResumableTool) }` comes first, then `has_output && Completed|Failed => Keep`. The design's file_changes for closers.rs lists rule 1 as has_output, then contradicts it in the same paragraph.
findings.suggested_fix: State one order: 1 browser_agent => Close(NotResumableTool); 2 has_output => Keep; 3 workspace lost => WorkspaceStateLost; 4 Completed|Failed => ResultLost; 5 NotRun => Redispatch; 6 Reserved|Unknown => effect UnknownOutcome, read Redispatch; 7 None => effect UnknownOutcome, read Redispatch.

findings.issue: The executor-to-gateway refusal contract changes, but s7c-v2's interface item 3 (the executor refusal tokens and CONTINUE_FRAME_REFUSALS, 19 entries) and item 4 ('every refusal returns before heartbeat_managed_agent_run') are not amended explicitly. S7b v3 adds PermissionDenied 'resume_forbidden', FailedPrecondition 'not_resumable' (RunEnded) and the ZDR catalogue status, none of which is in s7c-v2's list. It also adds post-heartbeat refusals (fence, pre-reserve). s7c-v2 notes that the committed PermissionDenied arm terminalizes the run. If S7c does not list resume_forbidden for the pre-consumed regime, a revoked member's continue either collapses to continue_refused or hits a terminalizing auth arm, and the invariant 'no executor refusal terminalizes the run' does not hold end to end. The token is also named 'durable_mutation_forbidden', but the catalogue kind trailer is 'zdr_durable_mutation_forbidden', and the status message is the catalogue's message, not a closed token.
findings.evidence: In s7c-v2 interfaces, 'WHAT S7c NEEDS FROM S7b', item 3 lists FailedPrecondition tokens without resume_forbidden, not_resumable or the catalogue status, and item 4 says 'Every refusal returns ... BEFORE heartbeat_managed_agent_run'. In mp-contracts zdr_refusal.rs: `pub const DURABLE_MUTATION_FORBIDDEN: &str = "zdr_durable_mutation_forbidden"`, and grpc_status puts it on KIND_TRAILER with self.message().
findings.suggested_fix: Add an amendments_to_prior_specs entry that rewrites s7c-v2 items 3 and 4: the three new tokens (with their gRPC codes), the trailer-keyed catalogue refusal, and the two post-heartbeat refusals (resume_checkpoint_unavailable, continuation_already_consumed). State that a pre-consumed PermissionDenied resume_forbidden must map to a non-terminalizing approval_spent frame. In classify_claim and the ledger-read mapping, re-emit the received catalogue status instead of rewriting it to DURABLE_MUTATION_FORBIDDEN. Name it by its catalogue kind.

findings.issue: The guard that the executor never reads AgentResume.segment_no covers only grpc.rs and agent.rs. restore_in_place in resume.rs takes `resume: &pb::AgentResume`, and resume.rs legitimately reads `.segment_no` on the fold and the claim response, so a rogue `resume.segment_no` read there would not be caught.
findings.evidence: builder_and_validator_violations: `for (name, code) in [("grpc.rs", &grpc), ("agent.rs", &agent)] { if code.text.contains(".segment_no") ...`
findings.suggested_fix: Add a resume.rs check for `\bresume\.segment_no\b` (and any AgentResume binding) to in_place_writer_violations, with a must_flag mutation.

findings.issue: The same denial gets different tokens. A PermissionDenied or Unauthenticated on the claim or the ledger read becomes resume_forbidden (F9). The same denial on the fence goes through fold::classify_status to Refused(Denied) and becomes resume_checkpoint_unavailable (F18). An operator or client cannot tell a revoked Space member apart from a store outage at the fence.
findings.evidence: fold.rs classify_status: `(Code::PermissionDenied | Code::Unauthenticated, _) => SaveError::Refused(RefusedBy::Denied)`. The design maps every fence Err to Refusal::CheckpointUnavailable.
findings.suggested_fix: Map SaveError::Refused(RefusedBy::Denied) and NotPersistent from save_fence to Forbidden and DurableMutationForbidden, consistent with section E/G. Otherwise, document the asymmetry in the failure matrix.

findings.issue: F22 and the sweep wording rely on SESSION_CORE_TOOL_LEDGER_SWEEP_ENABLED, which is not part of the coupled flip. With the sweep off, a reserved release row whose dispatch crashed stays `reserved`. Safety holds because L1 refuses on any row, but F22's 'the sweep makes it unknown_outcome' is conditional.
findings.evidence: tool_ledger.rs `const ENABLED_ENV: &str = "SESSION_CORE_TOOL_LEDGER_SWEEP_ENABLED"`, default off, and it is a separate switch_table row.
findings.suggested_fix: Qualify F22 ('with the sweep on'), or add the sweep to the coupled-flip list and comment.

spec.slice: S7c v3 - the GATEWAY, session-core and BFF/SPA half of the in-place resume, against HEAD 7a8e6cce, with lead decisions D1-D11 applied. Four build units that each compile and pass alone: S7c-0 (plan-grant defect, gateway only, no S7b dependency), S7c-A (omit_call proto + session-core spend-only consume with recovery renewal + resumable predicate + gateway pure unwired pieces + BFF closed-code relay + SPA contract; no S7b dependency), S7c-B (gateway wiring after S7b and after A5: pre-consume in one detached task, loop-mode hint, typed non-terminalizing frames gated on the gateway's OWN local knowledge that it pre-consumed, contract guards, coupled-flip pins). NO attestation field. The gateway keeps stating space_id empty.
spec.summary:
v3 re-verifies every v2 claim against committed source (git show semantics; the working tree is clean at HEAD 7a8e6cce; sse.rs, orchestration_store.rs, run_service_grpc.rs, terminalization.rs, orchestration_grpc.rs and the BFF files are unchanged since 2aafc0b5, so v2's code facts hold) and applies the lead decisions.

D1 (no attestation): AgentResume.consumed_by_gateway is dropped entirely; execution.proto is not touched. The committed executor rule already does what D1 needs: prepare_resume accepts consumed.consumed || (already_consumed && same_claim && replay_is_fenced) with replay_is_fenced = effect::ledger_enabled(). A gateway pre-consume followed by the executor's own consume (same claim hash, ledger on) is therefore an allowed replay. A second request, same token or another, loses the gateway consume and gets 409 continuation_already_consumed before it reaches the executor. The typed approval_spent frames are gated on a local fact: the launch closure ran, which only happens after consumed == true, so the stream is opened with ApprovalSpend::SpentByGateway. Nothing the executor says or a client sends can switch the typed arms on. The gateway resume switch, the executor resume switch, EXECUTION_EFFECT_LEDGER_ENABLED, AGENT_CONTINUE_AFTER_APPROVAL_ENABLED (both services) and the checkpoint switches are one coupled flip; the hard rule is that the gateway switch is never on unless the executor's ledger and continue switches are on. spec.approach:
VERIFIED STATE (committed source, function names, not line numbers). Unchanged since 2aafc0b5: model-gateway sse.rs, http_routes.rs; session-core orchestration_store.rs, orchestration_grpc.rs, run_service_grpc.rs, terminalization.rs; the BFF upstream.rs and orchestration.rs.
