V1. model-gateway sse.rs. continue_run: continuation_gate, continue_persistent_gate (only with the switch on), body check 400 continue_incomplete, bearer check 401 missing_bearer, require_durable_run_owner_with_token, get_run, get_approval, continue_preflight (7 arguments, refuses a consumed approval and any mode other than loop), then agentic_run_stream with space_id String::new(), AgentRoute::default(), detail.goal, Vec::new() tools and Some(continue_resume(approval_id, claim_token)). continue_resume builds the ONE AgentResume literal: mode "segment", segment_no 0. agentic_run_stream has two callers (invoke_stream_sse and continue_run). Inside its spawned task it sends the connected frame (a json! payload with ok, run_id, thread_id, request_id), then runs approved_plan_context whenever plan_mode is false, which includes a /continue; approved_plan_block_for calls PlanModeStore::take_approved_plan (removes the in-memory grant pointer) and then claims the plan APPROVED to EXECUTING; the block is prepended to the goal in build_run_agent_request. Dispatch arms: Err(DeadlineExpired) and Ok(Err(join)) and the final Ok(Ok(Err(status))) each publish RUN_DISPATCH_DEGRADED and send agent_dispatch_unavailable (retryable true); InvalidArgument | Unauthenticated | PermissionDenied terminalize through terminalize_agent_dispatch_rejection_authenticated and send agent_dispatch_rejected; dispatch_never_reached_execution_core (a connect-phase Unavailable whose source chain holds ConnectionRefused, HostUnreachable, NetworkUnreachable or AddrNotAvailable) terminalizes as Unreachable. spawn_run_dispatch makes one tokio::spawn around one execution_client.run_agent call. follow_agentic_run ignores a closed client channel (let _ = tx.send) and the dispatch handle is a detached JoinHandle, so once launch returns the dispatch no longer depends on the handler. The gateway's execution channel is Endpoint::connect_lazy with a connect timeout and no retry layer (state.rs lazy_channel). In sse.rs and http_routes.rs the type named VerifiedModelBearer is an alias of auth::VerifiedSessionBearer (the aud=session-core user bearer, Clone, Arc<str>); it is exactly the credential the executor receives as its session bearer, so the gateway's consume and the executor's replay consume use one credential.

V2. execution-core. enforce_resume (grpc.rs) already accepts mode "segment" and "loop" and refuses continue_disabled (FailedPrecondition) and resume_incomplete (InvalidArgument); it runs before run_agent_with_route. prepare_resume (agent.rs) is the ONLY Rust ConsumeApprovalRequest struct literal in the workspace (no ..Default::default()); doubles implement the trait with `_` requests; no Go code outside gen builds one. Its replay rule is replay_is_fenced = effect::ledger_enabled(). Refusals return before heartbeat_managed_agent_run (which discards HeartbeatManagedRunResponse and maps any failure to Unavailable "managed terminalization heartbeat unavailable") and leave the run non-terminal. resume.rs Refusal is today only authority_widened, authority_space_mismatch, authority_route_mismatch (FailedPrecondition, message = token). run_pause_mode returns "" (cold) for any run with a Space or a provider hint.

V3. session-core. consume_approval (store) is one transaction: CONSUME_APPROVAL_SQL (compare-and-set; requires retention_class persistent, run not ended, status granted, continuation_mode non-empty, unconsumed, unexpired, a descriptor row), then read_consumed_call (decrypt) on the winning branch and on a same-claim replay; a replay is answered consumed false, already_consumed true, same_claim true with the call only to the claimant; a different token gets already_consumed with no call; run-ended or non-persistent gives NotFound. The handler requires orchestration:write, a user-bound credential, authorize_run_owner(Mutate), and broadcasts RunResumedAfterApproval only when consumed. Recovery: claim_due_recovery selects obligations in state open with deadline_at <= now() and next_attempt_at <= now() (or processing with an expired lease), on a non-terminal run, with NOT EXISTS an approval in requested|granted with consumed_at IS NULL; has_pending_approval has no expires_at test; release_recovery_for_activity moves only next_attempt_at; run_recovery_worker sleeps 1 second; heartbeat_managed_run is the only writer of deadline_at (now + MANAGED_DEADLINE_SECS = 900, a private const) and the executor discards its answer. CONSUME_APPROVAL_SQL never touches managed_run_terminalization_outbox (run_id primary key, org_id column present). So a spent click makes a run recoverable within about a second whenever the human took more than 15 minutes; at HEAD stage 1 the window is milliseconds, a gateway pre-consume widens it to the whole gateway-to-executor path. RUN_SELECT (shared by GetRun and both ListRuns branches; the Space branch appends JOIN threads t after the FROM, the thread-less branch appends WHERE; aliases r, lc, e, c, t, st are taken) ends with LEFT JOIN run_loop_checkpoints lc and a test pins that ending and forbids projecting ciphertext, fold_digest, authority_digest, claim_token_hash. row_to_detail returns resumable to any viewer and park_reason only to the owner or a service; run_detail_value in model-gateway http_routes is an allowlist without either. The pause approval's idempotency_key is format!("{run_id}:{step_id}") and equals the pause fold's pause_ref (execution-core already asserts approval.idempotency_key == pending.pause_ref in its pause test); the unique index on approvals is (org_id, user_id, idempotency_key) WHERE idempotency_key <> ''.

V4. BFF. proxy_sse_stream_with_data_plane (16 parameters, trailing zdr) turns every upstream status >= 400 into model_error (401 into unauthorized) without reading the body. Callers: chat/shared.rs (2), chat/streams.rs (1), orchestration.rs continue_run (1), plus the wrappers proxy_sse_stream and proxy_sse_stream_with_session inside upstream.rs. continue_run in the BFF has no retry wrapper. tests/sse_relay_no_allowlist.rs scans only the relay function body (no ChatEvent name as a quoted string, the bytes_stream line, the verbatim yield, sse_transport_error_event). envelope::error takes code: &'static str. SPA: readSseStream turns a non-OK response into ApiError(message, status, code) from {error:{code,message}}; continueRun rethrows it; chat.run.continue exists in action-registry.ts with input schema runId, approvalId, claimToken and no UI caller.

V5. Contract tests that constrain this design (execution-core tests/durable_loop_contract.rs): builder_and_validator_violations anchors on the regex mode: "segment".to_owned() inside continue_resume and on exactly one segment_no: 0 and one use of the word segment_no in gateway sse.rs production text; single_resume_violations needs exactly one AgentResume literal; the posture scans take continue_run's body as the text from "pub(crate) async fn continue_run(" to the next "\n#[cfg(test)]", so every new gateway item must sit BEFORE continue_run and none may name segment_no; zdr_posture and tests/zdr_posture_matrix.rs require continue_persistent_gate( in the handler and the text between continue_preflight( and ).map_err to contain continue_turn_is_persistent(&claims).

LEAD DECISIONS AND THEIR CONSEQUENCES (applied, not reopened)
D1. Coupled flip. Required relation: gateway EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED on implies executor EXECUTION_EFFECT_LEDGER_ENABLED on and AGENT_CONTINUE_AFTER_APPROVAL_ENABLED on at gateway and executor. In-place additionally needs executor EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED, EXECUTION_LOOP_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED and SESSION_CORE_LOOP_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED; with those off the loop hint downgrades to stage 1 and everything still works. Recommended flip order: session-core checkpoint, executor ledger + checkpoint + continue, then the resume switch on gateway and executor together. Pins added in S7c-B2: a guard holding the executor replay rule (accepts a same-claim replay only through effect::ledger_enabled()) and the gateway's single loop_resume_enabled() read as one pair, mutation-tested both ways (replay accepted without the ledger is unsafe; replay refused always would make every pre-consume lose); switch_table rows (S7b owns them; verified present before B1). Mismatch behaviours are in the failure matrix. A gateway-side mirror of the ledger switch (so a mismatch degrades to the committed path) was considered and NOT taken: it would add a second gateway switch and D1 asks for a described, recognisable failure instead.
D2. The request states nothing wider than the pause: space_id "", route default, rung unspecified (dispatch_autonomy_rung(resuming) already discards the thread grant), floor 0, plan false, tools empty. continue_space_scope_unsupported and the authority_* tokens stay in the frame vocabulary and are marked unreachable through the gateway today.
D3. After a won claim a fallback or refusal leaves the fold resuming for its 120 s lease and then claimable again; the gateway never closes it; the resumable predicate (D5) is what stops it advertising itself.
D4. S7c-0 = plan_context_wanted(plan_mode, resuming) = !plan_mode && !resuming gating approved_plan_context in agentic_run_stream. A /continue never calls take_approved_plan or claims the plan, so the grant keeps its TTL for the next ordinary run. It changes behaviour only on a route that needs AGENT_CONTINUE_AFTER_APPROVAL_ENABLED, so with every switch off nothing changes.
D5. See file_changes A3. resumable = old rule AND NOT (fold kind pause AND the approval keyed by pause_ref is consumed).
D6. S7b step 6 (the release reserved through the ledger whatever its class) must be deployed before the gateway switch flips, because after a pre-consume every executor consume is a replay and a read-class release would otherwise have no ledger fence. The gateway's structural guarantee (one launch per won consume, no retry layer) makes a duplicate RunAgent impossible; D6 makes it harmless as well.
D7, D11: follow-ups and open items only.
D8. Spend-only consume kept: omit_call = 7; session-core neither reads nor decrypts the descriptor (winning branch or replay branch); response carries consumed, already_consumed, same_claim only; the winning transaction renews the run's managed obligation (state open, deadline_at now + 900 s, next_attempt_at now, lease cleared, only states open and processing, scoped by run_id and org_id; zero rows is not an error; a database error rolls the whole consume back so the click is not spent). Only a WON spend-only consume renews. The executor's own full consume (omit_call false) never renews, so the switch-off path is byte-identical.
D9. A retry after a dropped or ambiguous consume is 409 continuation_already_consumed by the standing decision. continue_unreachable does not terminalize. After a 503 continue_unavailable, a same-token retry either wins (the consume had rolled back) or gets 409, which then means spent: follow the run's events.
D10. Deploy and flip order as stated in the slice.

A. ORDER OF EVERY RPC AFTER S7c (resume switch on; with it off see the last paragraph)
BFF: mint model, data-plane, inference, execution and session bearers (auth-core), read org ZDR, POST gateway /continue (no retry). Gateway: 1 continuation_gate. 2 continue_persistent_gate (ZDR or waived refused 409 not_resumable before anything is read). 3 body check (400 continue_incomplete). 4 bearer check (401 missing_bearer). 5 require_durable_run_owner_with_token. 6 GetRun (status, goal, thread_id, resumable). 7 GetApproval. 8 continue_preflight (local; refuses a consumed approval; no consume yet). 9 the loop switch is read ONCE (loop_resume_enabled()); mode = resume_mode_for(on, detail.resumable); spend = approval_spend_for(on); ONE launch closure is built holding the single agentic_run_stream call. With the switch on: ONE detached task (spawn_consume_then_launch) calls ConsumeApproval with the user session bearer (step_id "", action_fingerprint "", claim_token as sent, omit_call true), bounded by a 10 second timeout; session-core in one transaction compare-and-sets, renews the obligation and commits; only consumed == true runs the launch closure; the handler awaits a oneshot. 10 inside the stream task: connected frame (carrying approval_spent true when spend is SpentByGateway), NO approved-plan claim, spawn_run_dispatch, RunAgent, orchestration tail. 11 executor (S7b): enforce_resume, ConsumeApproval replay (same claim, ledger on, reads the descriptor), stage 1 or the in-place claim, then the heartbeat.
Resume switch off: steps 1 to 8 unchanged; step 9 is just Ok(launch()) with mode "segment" and spend NotSpent (no pre-consume, no spawn); step 10 loses only the plan claim (D4); step 11 as committed; every failure arm is the committed one, byte for byte. Exceptions to byte identity, stated honestly: (a) no plan claim and no plan block in goal on a /continue (S7c-0; the route needs the continue switch); (b) the BFF relays eight closed codes instead of model_error (A5); (c) RunDetail.resumable excludes consumed pause folds (A3, no consumer today); (d) the gateway's vocabulary for the same refusals is unchanged.

B. PRE-CONSUME RULES AND THE DETACHED TASK
Pure map preconsume_refusal(Result<bool, tonic::Status>) -> Result<(), PreconsumeRefusal> where PreconsumeRefusal is Closed(StatusCode, &'static str) or Status(tonic::Status): Ok(true) proceeds; Ok(false) (already consumed, whatever the claim, the same token included) is 409 continuation_already_consumed; NotFound is 404 approval_not_found; FailedPrecondition with message approval_not_granted, approval_expired or approval_not_resumable is 409 with that code, any other FailedPrecondition 409 not_resumable; InvalidArgument is 400 continue_incomplete; PermissionDenied and Unauthenticated become Status(..) and the handler answers crate::http_routes::grpc_status_to_http (the same flat or typed ZDR body the owner check and the reads already return; this is the one documented place a session-core message text reaches the caller, it is closed session-core wording and never the claim token, which session-core never puts in a status message); EVERY other code (Unavailable, DeadlineExceeded, Internal, Unknown, Cancelled, Aborted, ResourceExhausted, Unimplemented, anything new) is the catch-all 503 continue_unavailable, ambiguous by definition because the consume may have committed. Logs carry the gRPC code and run_id only.
Detach. trait ApprovalConsumer { fn consume(&self, ConsumeApprovalRequest) -> impl Future<Output = Result<bool, tonic::Status>> + Send } (the file already uses this trait style for ApprovedPlanSource). GrpcApprovalConsumer owns a clone of state.orchestration_client and a clone of the session bearer; consume builds the request with authenticated_session_request, wraps the RPC in tokio::time::timeout(PRECONSUME_TIMEOUT = 10 s, a constant, no new env) and maps Elapsed to Status::deadline_exceeded; it returns response.consumed and reads no other field. async fn consume_then_launch<C: ApprovalConsumer, T>(&C, request, launch: impl FnOnce() -> T) -> Result<T, PreconsumeRefusal> is the pure sequencing unit. fn spawn_consume_then_launch<C, T>(consumer: C, request, launch: impl FnOnce() -> T + Send + 'static) -> oneshot::Receiver<Result<T, PreconsumeRefusal>> (C: ApprovalConsumer + Send + 'static, T: Send + 'static) holds the ONLY tokio::spawn of the path: it creates the oneshot, spawns an async move block that runs consume_then_launch(&consumer, request, launch).await and sends the outcome (a closed receiver is ignored), and returns the receiver. A client disconnect drops the receiver, never the task, so a won consume is always followed by the launch; the stream task's sends are already ignored on a closed channel. continue_run: switch off, Ok(launch()); switch on, match spawn_consume_then_launch(..).await { Ok(Ok(sse)) => Ok(sse), Ok(Err(Closed(s, c))) => continue_error(s, c), Ok(Err(Status(st))) => grpc_status_to_http(&st), Err(_) => continue_error(503, continue_unavailable) }. Residual window, honest: a gateway process crash, a timeout that fires after the server committed, or a rolling restart between the consume and the RunAgent send leaves a spent click and a non-terminal run until the renewed deadline ends; /continue streams are not registered in the drain registry today (pre-existing), so the detached task is not either (follow-up).
Deploy skew: an old session-core ignores omit_call, returns the decrypted call to the gateway (which reads only .consumed) and does not renew, so deploy session-core before the gateway.

C. MODE CHOICE AND THE RESUMABLE HINT
resume_mode_for(resume_enabled: bool, resumable: bool) -> &'static str returns "loop" only when both are true, else "segment"; these two literals are the only place a mode is named in the gateway; segment_no stays 0; step_id, tool_name, action_fingerprint and brief stay empty. The hint is advisory: the executor decides at claim time and a wrong hint costs a stage-1 fallback, never a refusal. RunDetail.resumable accuracy (D5): RUN_SELECT gains
  CASE WHEN lc.kind = 'pause' THEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM approvals ap WHERE ap.org_id = r.org_id AND ap.user_id = r.user_id AND ap.run_id = r.id AND ap.idempotency_key = lc.pause_ref AND ap.consumed_at IS NOT NULL) END AS fold_pause_consumed
placed before the FROM (alias ap is unused elsewhere, the LEFT JOIN stays the last line; the CASE confines the probe to rows that have a pause fold, and the user_id predicate lets the unique index serve it). RunRow gains fold_pause_consumed: Option<bool> (the three RunRow literals in run_service_grpc tests get None). row_to_detail: resumable = old rule AND NOT (fold_kind == Some("pause") AND fold_pause_consumed == Some(true)). A mismatch of keys costs one fallback, never safety. park_reason logic is unchanged.

D. THE THREAD'S APPROVED PLAN (S7c-0)
plan_context = if plan_context_wanted(plan_mode, resume.is_some()) { approved_plan_context(..).await } else { None }. A continuation never calls take_approved_plan, never claims the plan, never injects it into goal, and never uses granted_rung (spawn_run_dispatch still calls state.plan_mode.granted_rung, a read-only lookup whose result dispatch_autonomy_rung discards for a resume).

E. FAILURE CLASSIFICATION, GATED BY LOCAL SPEND (D1)
enum ApprovalSpend { NotSpent, SpentByGateway } is a new trailing parameter of agentic_run_stream (invoke_stream_sse passes NotSpent). approval_spend_for(resume_enabled) is pure; continue_run passes SpentByGateway only on the pre-consume path, inside the launch closure that runs only after consumed == true. With NotSpent every arm is the committed one, byte for byte. With SpentByGateway: pure classify_continue_dispatch_failure(&tonic::Status) -> ContinueDispatchFailure { Refused(&'static str), Unreachable, Unknown }. Order: (1) if mp_contracts::zdr_refusal::Refusal::from_status(&status) is Some, Refused("durable_mutation_forbidden") when its code is the durable-mutation one, else Refused("continue_refused") (never the message); (2) NotFound is Refused("approval_not_found"); (3) FailedPrecondition, Aborted, InvalidArgument, PermissionDenied or Unauthenticated with a message exactly in CONTINUE_EXECUTOR_MESSAGE_TOKENS is Refused(that token), any other message there is Refused("continue_refused") (never echoed); (4) dispatch_never_reached_execution_core(&status) is Unreachable; (5) everything else (other Unavailable, DeadlineExceeded, Internal, Cancelled, the follow deadline, a join error) is Unknown. continue_failure_event(request_id, run_id, &ContinueDispatchFailure) -> Event is ChatEvent::Error { code, message = code with spaces, retryable: false } with run_id and approval_spent: true added to the payload (the pattern agent_dispatch_unavailable_event uses). Refused(t) sends t; Unreachable sends continue_unreachable; Unknown sends continue_outcome_unknown; a local RunAgent request-construction failure sends continue_refused. NONE of them terminalizes. RUN_DISPATCH_DEGRADED is still published for Unreachable and Unknown, not for Refused. dispatch_unknown_event(spend, request_id, run_id) returns the old agent_dispatch_unavailable_event for NotSpent and continue_outcome_unknown for SpentByGateway; the three agent_dispatch_unavailable_event sites (deadline, join error, final ambiguous arm) call it. The new arm Ok(Ok(Err(status))) if spend.is_spent() sits BEFORE is_confirmed_agent_dispatch_rejection; the Err(error) request-construction branch gets an early path for the spent case before its terminalization. Logs add the closed token and run_id; never the claim token, the approval content or an upstream message.
What a pre-consumed continuation leaves behind: run non-terminal, approval spent, obligation renewed at the consume, so session-core recovery terminalizes it 15 minutes after the consume if nothing heartbeats. Post-response frames (agent_run_failed, agent_run_state_unknown, agent_run_output_unavailable, subscription failures) keep their committed retryable values; the connected frame's approval_spent true is what tells the client not to re-POST.
connected_payload(run_id, thread_id, request_id, spend) -> Value is a tiny extraction of the inline json!; for NotSpent it is byte-identical to the committed payload; for SpentByGateway it adds approval_spent: true.

F. CLIENT-VISIBLE VOCABULARIES (closed, test-pinned, gateway-owned)
HTTP, CONTINUE_HTTP_REFUSALS (10): continue_disabled 409, not_resumable 409, continue_incomplete 400, missing_bearer 401, approval_not_found 404, approval_not_granted 409, approval_expired 409, approval_not_resumable 409, continuation_already_consumed 409, continue_unavailable 503. The BFF relays 8 (all but continue_incomplete, which its own guard preempts, and missing_bearer, which maps to unauthorized). Other statuses (owner check, reads, ZDR typed refusals, a consume PermissionDenied or Unauthenticated) keep grpc_status_to_http's body, and every such HTTP error happens before any consume, so it says not spent. Any HTTP response that is not 200 is not spent except continuation_already_consumed (spent, by this client earlier or by another click) and continue_unavailable (unknown).
Stream, CONTINUE_FRAME_REFUSALS (22) in three groups. Message tokens carried by the executor (CONTINUE_EXECUTOR_MESSAGE_TOKENS, 17): continue_disabled, resume_incomplete, continuation_already_consumed, approval_not_granted, approval_expired, approval_not_resumable, approval_action_mismatch, approval_snapshot_mismatch, not_releasable, authority_widened, authority_space_mismatch, authority_route_mismatch, continue_space_scope_unsupported, continue_in_progress, resume_checkpoint_unavailable, not_resumable, resume_forbidden. Code-derived (2): approval_not_found (NotFound), durable_mutation_forbidden (zdr trailer). Gateway-made (3): continue_refused, continue_unreachable, continue_outcome_unknown. Reachable through the gateway today: continue_disabled, continuation_already_consumed (the mismatched-flip signature), approval_not_resumable, approval_snapshot_mismatch, not_releasable, resume_checkpoint_unavailable, continue_in_progress, not_resumable, resume_forbidden, approval_not_found (run ended mid-way), durable_mutation_forbidden, authority_widened only if the pause held a rung the gateway never states (not reachable), and the three gateway ones. Unreachable and kept as defence in depth: resume_incomplete, approval_not_granted, approval_expired, approval_action_mismatch (the replay branch of consume never checks them; the gateway sends no hints), authority_space_mismatch, authority_route_mismatch, continue_space_scope_unsupported. These frames exist ONLY for a pre-consumed continuation and always carry approval_spent: true and retryable false. Meaning: the approval is spent, no retry with a new token, follow the run through its events. The committed frames on a switch-off continuation (agent_dispatch_unavailable, agent_dispatch_rejected, agent_dispatch_unreachable, session_terminalization_failed) say nothing about the approval and the contract says so (a retry with a new token is permitted by the committed rules).

G. BFF
proxy_sse_stream_with_data_plane gains a trailing relayed_errors: &'static [(&'static str, u16, &'static str)] (code, upstream status, fixed message). The two wrappers, chat/shared.rs (2 sites) and chat/streams.rs (1 site) pass &[]; orchestration.rs continue_run passes CONTINUE_RELAYED_ERRORS. WHAT S7C NEEDS FROM S7B (the interface the two designs must fit)
1. AgentResume.mode: only "segment" (stage 1) and "loop" (stage 2); the stage is chosen ONLY by this field. enforce_resume at HEAD already accepts exactly these two. The gateway sends "loop" only with its switch on and RunDetail.resumable. The executor downgrades "loop" to stage 1 when its own resume, checkpoint or ledger switch is off, or for a ZDR or waived run: a downgrade, never a refusal. segment_no is 0 and ignored; step_id, tool_name, action_fingerprint and brief are empty. There is NO new AgentResume field: consumed_by_gateway is dropped (D1), field 9 stays reserved, field 10 stays unused.
2. The replay rule (D1), identical in both stages, independent of the executor's resume switch: the executor's own ConsumeApproval proceeds when consumed.consumed || (consumed.already_consumed && consumed.same_claim && effect::ledger_enabled()); otherwise FailedPrecondition continuation_already_consumed. S7b moves this rule verbatim into consume_for_resume and must neither add an attestation nor accept a replay with the ledger off. After a gateway pre-consume EVERY executor consume is such a replay (consumed false, already_consumed true, same_claim true, the descriptor returned to the claimant).
3. Closed refusal tokens the executor may return after the consume, as gRPC code plus exact message: FailedPrecondition continuation_already_consumed | approval_not_resumable | approval_snapshot_mismatch | not_releasable | authority_widened | authority_space_mismatch | authority_route_mismatch | continue_space_scope_unsupported | resume_checkpoint_unavailable | not_resumable (run ended, from the claim) | continue_disabled | approval_not_granted | approval_expired | approval_action_mismatch; Aborted continue_in_progress; InvalidArgument resume_incomplete; PermissionDenied resume_forbidden (claim Space revocation); a ZDR trailer refusal (zdr_refusal kind zdr_durable_mutation_forbidden; the gateway keys on the trailer, not the message, because the message is a catalogue sentence); NotFound (session-core text) for an approval or run that vanished. Anything else reaches the client as continue_refused: safe and unhelpful; a new token needs a row in CONTINUE_EXECUTOR_MESSAGE_TOKENS and the guard in B2. A claim failure after a won consume is a fallback to stage 1, not a refusal (D3, fold not closed), except the fatal ones above.
4. Consume and launch are one detached task owned by spawn_consume_then_launch (the only tokio::spawn of the path): a client disconnect cannot spend an approval without RunAgent being sent. Test- and source-guarded.

A won spend-only consume renews the run's managed obligation deadline in the same transaction (state open, deadline now + MANAGED_DEADLINE_SECS, lease cleared, only open and processing states, scoped by run_id and org_id); a replay, a lost race or a full consume never renews; a database error rolls the consume back.

The gateway never holds a consumed call's content: omit_call is set, session-core does not read, decrypt or return it, one boolean is read, and logs carry the gRPC code, a closed token and run_id only, never the claim token, call content or an upstream message.

The only place an upstream message text can reach a caller from the consume path is grpc_status_to_http for PermissionDenied and Unauthenticated, the same body the owner check and the reads return; every other consume failure is a closed code.

The typed spent arms are gated on the gateway's own local knowledge that it pre-consumed (ApprovalSpend::SpentByGateway, set only inside the launch closure that runs after consumed == true), never on resume.is_some() and never on any executor field; a continuation the gateway did not pre-consume keeps the committed arms byte for byte.

The gateway never terminalizes a pre-consumed continuation; every pre-consumed failure frame is retryable false, carries run_id and approval_spent true, and is never agent_dispatch_*; the connected frame of a pre-consumed continuation carries approval_spent true, and for NotSpent it is byte-identical to the committed payload.

The mode the gateway sends is 'loop' only with the switch on and RunDetail.resumable, else 'segment'; no other value; segment_no 0; hint fields empty; there is NO attestation field; a wrong hint costs a stage-1 fallback and nothing else.
A continuation never reads, claims or injects the thread's approved plan or grant and states no rung, floor, Space, route or tools.

RunDetail.resumable stays readable by every reader of the run at RPC level (a boolean) and never reaches a browser (run_detail_value is an allowlist); park_reason stays owner-or-service; a pause fold whose approval is consumed is not resumable.

The BFF relays only a (code, status) pair from the closed list with its own fixed message; every other upstream error is model_error or unauthorized; SSE bytes are relayed untouched and the relay body still passes tests/sse_relay_no_allowlist.rs.

The executor, not the gateway, owns what a continuation runs: tools, authority, mode and the approved call come from the paused snapshot; the executor's consume replay is the only reader of the descriptor.

With EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED off, the RPC sequence to session-core's approval store and to execution-core and the RunAgent bytes of /continue are the committed ones, with the stated exceptions (no plan claim, BFF code relay, the resumable projection).

One /continue route, one AgentResume literal (continue_resume), one segment_no literal, one ConsumeApprovalRequest literal in the gateway, one agentic_run_stream call in continue_run, one loop_resume_enabled() read in continue_run.

Coupled flip: the gateway resume switch is never on unless the executor's ledger and continue switches are on; all switches default off in compose; the resume switch is the same variable on gateway and executor.

The workspace builds after every commit: the omit_call proto field and the executor literal land together; S7c-B lands only after S7b's symbols exist and after A5; the builder guard re-point lands with the continue_resume arity change.
The gateway consumes with the same session bearer the executor later receives; no bearer, token or claim token is persisted or logged; the vocabularies contain closed tokens only.

failure_matrix: BFF cannot mint a bearer (auth-core down) | nothing | existing delegated_auth_unavailable | nothing consumed; retry freely.
BFF cannot reach model-gateway | nothing | 502 upstream_unavailable | nothing consumed; the same token may retry (the BFF has no retry wrapper on /continue).

Gateway: switch off, ZDR or waived turn, blank body, missing bearer | nothing read or written | 409 continue_disabled, 409 not_resumable, 400 continue_incomplete, 401 missing_bearer | nothing consumed.
Owner check, GetRun or GetApproval fails | nothing | grpc_status_to_http status with its flat body, BFF model_error | nothing consumed.

Preflight refuses (run ended, approval of another run, not granted, cold approval, already consumed) | nothing | 409 not_resumable | 404 approval_not_found | 409 approval_not_granted | 409 continuation_already_consumed | nothing consumed; for a consumed approval the other continuation owns it.

Pre-consume lost: another claim won first, or the same token again | the winner's state | 409 continuation_already_consumed (before any stream) | session-core compare-and-set; this request never reaches RunAgent; no renewal for the loser.
Pre-consume NotFound (run ended, lost retention, approval gone between preflight and consume) | nothing | 404 approval_not_found | nothing consumed, nothing renewed; discloses nothing about the run.

Pre-consume FailedPrecondition not_granted, expired, not_resumable, or any other | nothing | 409 with that code, or 409 not_resumable | nothing consumed, nothing renewed (an approval that expired between preflight and consume leaves the run as it was).
Pre-consume PermissionDenied or Unauthenticated | nothing | the grpc_status_to_http body (403 or 401, possibly the typed ZDR body) | nothing consumed.

Pre-consume transport failure, timeout (10 s) or any other code | consumed_at possibly set (unknown), deadline possibly renewed | 503 continue_unavailable | nothing ran; if it committed the click is spent, a same-token retry is 409 which then means spent: follow the run's events; recovery ends the run 15 minutes after the consume.

Pre-consume renewal statement fails (database error) | the whole consume transaction rolls back; the click is NOT spent | 503 continue_unavailable | the same token may retry and wins; the gateway cannot tell this from a committed consume and reports ambiguity.

Client disconnects during the consume RPC | consume possibly committed | nobody (client gone) | spawn_consume_then_launch finishes the consume and still launches RunAgent; the continuation runs; the user reconnects through run events; a retry is 409.

Gateway process dies, or is rolled, after the consume committed and before RunAgent is sent | consumed_at set, deadline renewed to consume + 15 min, paused fold untouched, run non-terminal | broken connection (BFF 502 or a transport event) | nothing ran; retry is 409; recovery terminalizes about 15 minutes after the consume and purges the fold. Honest residual window (the detached task is not in the drain registry).

Recovery worker polls between the consume and the executor heartbeat | nothing | nothing | the renewed deadline makes the run ineligible for 15 minutes, so the executor's replay and heartbeat always find a live run.

RunAgent request cannot be built locally after a pre-consume | spent, nothing ran | frame continue_refused, retryable false, approval_spent true | not terminalized; recovery 15 minutes after the consume. (Not pre-consumed: the committed terminalizing arm.)

Executor unreachable after a pre-consume (connect refused, or DNS failure for a stopped container) | spent, nothing ran, run non-terminal | frame continue_unreachable (connect refused) or continue_outcome_unknown (other transport), retryable false, approval_spent true | RUN_DISPATCH_DEGRADED published; recovery 15 minutes after the consume; retry is 409. Not pre-consumed (switch off): committed arm, run terminalized for a connect refusal, approval still unconsumed.

RunAgent outcome ambiguous after a pre-consume (reset after send, follow deadline, join error, executor heartbeat failure) | the continuation may be running | frame continue_outcome_unknown, retryable false, run_id, approval_spent true | do not retry; follow the run; the executor owns the receipt; closers and sweep decide unknown effects; no gateway terminalization. Not pre-consumed: committed agent_dispatch_unavailable.

Executor refuses before dispatching (any token of the 22) after a pre-consume | spent, run non-terminal, fold unchanged or resuming for its lease | frame with that token, approval_spent true | nothing ran; the executor returns before heartbeat or any terminal write; recovery after the renewed window.

Executor returns continuation_already_consumed after phase 2 (released step replayed) | another segment owns and runs the run | frame continuation_already_consumed, approval_spent true | the gateway does not terminalize (the spent arm precedes the confirmed-rejection arm); the committed arm would have failed a live run.

MISMATCHED FLIP A: gateway resume switch on, executor EXECUTION_EFFECT_LEDGER_ENABLED off | click spent by the gateway; the executor's same-claim replay is refused (replay_is_fenced false) | a 200 stream: connected frame with approval_spent true, then error continuation_already_consumed with approval_spent true and retryable false; gateway warn log with the token and run_id | operator signature: a stream-level (not HTTP) continuation_already_consumed, consumed_at set, no ledger row, run non-terminal until the 15 minute recovery. A duplicate click, by contrast, is an HTTP 409 before any stream. Fix: turn the executor ledger and continue switches on before the gateway switch; deploy order executor, session-core, gateway.

MISMATCHED FLIP B: gateway resume switch on, executor AGENT_CONTINUE_AFTER_APPROVAL_ENABLED off | click spent | frame continue_disabled, approval_spent true | enforce_resume refuses before the executor's consume but after the gateway's; recovery 15 minutes after the consume; flip both continue switches together.
Gateway resume switch on, executor resume switch off, ledger on | none | normal | the executor downgrades loop to stage 1 and accepts the replay (ledger on); no refusal.
Gateway on, session-core checkpoint switch off or no fold | none | normal | RunDetail.resumable is false so the gateway sends segment; stage 1.
Executor resume switch on, gateway off | none | normal | the committed behaviour: the executor consumes itself, no renewal beyond its own heartbeat (millisecond window as at HEAD).

New gateway with an old session-core | omit_call ignored, the call comes back to the gateway (read as .consumed only), no renewal | normal | deploy session-core before the gateway; the stale-deadline window is back until it is.

New gateway with a pre-S7b executor image | none if the ledger is on | normal | the committed executor accepts mode loop as stage 1 and accepts the replay with the ledger on; with the ledger off it is MISMATCHED FLIP A.
Executor completes | normal frames and done | the answer | one released ledger row under the new step id; the executor heartbeat renews the deadline as at HEAD.

Executor pauses again | new approval (step ids prefixed with the next segment) | awaiting_approval frame | a fresh /continue with the new approval and a new claim token; the fold exists only if the in-place writer is seeded.
Browser disconnects mid-stream after dispatch | run continues server side | nothing | the RunAgent task is detached; the thread shows the result.
BFF loses the upstream mid-stream | run continues | existing upstream_unavailable event | unchanged.
Two clicks at once, distinct tokens | one winner | one 200 stream and one 409 | the compare-and-set; one ledger row for the released call; one renewal.
Two clicks at once, same token | one winner | one 200 and one 409 (new) | pre-consume refuses the loser; closes the same-token gap.

Run cancelled or terminalized between the gateway consume and the executor replay | nothing more | frame approval_not_found, approval_spent true | the replay branch answers NotFound for an ended run; nothing runs.
Approved plan pending on the thread | untouched | nothing | the continuation never takes it (S7c-0).

Stale fold after a stage-1 continuation or an abandoned claim | the original pause fold stays until terminal purge | later continues use segment | the consumed-approval predicate makes resumable false; a wrong loop would cost one claim_not_claimable fallback.

Executor does not stop on heartbeat already_terminal (pre-existing, D7) | a run terminalized by another path can still have its approved call dispatched | the user sees a failed run although the effect ran | not caused by S7c, narrowed by the renewal; follow-up recorded.

findings.file: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/sse.rs (agentic_run_stream arms) and the binding 'a refused or replayed segment is a confirmed rejection, never a degraded dispatch'
findings.issue: The binding is honoured only for a gateway pre-consumed continuation. For every continuation the gateway did not pre-consume (resume switch off, AGENT_CONTINUE_AFTER_APPROVAL_ENABLED on) the design keeps the committed arms 'byte for byte'. There an executor refusal (continue_disabled, continuation_already_consumed on a same-claim replay with the ledger off, authority_widened, approval_snapshot_mismatch and so on) is a FailedPrecondition or Aborted status. It is not in is_confirmed_agent_dispatch_rejection, so it lands in the ambiguous arm. That arm publishes RUN_DISPATCH_DEGRADED and sends agent_dispatch_unavailable with retryable true, which is exactly a degraded dispatch for a refused or replayed segment. The design's own flag to the lead covers only 'do not terminalize'. It does not say the binding is knowingly unmet on the switch-off path, and the design lists that path under the byte-identical-with-switches-off rule.
findings.evidence: sse.rs is_confirmed_agent_dispatch_rejection matches only InvalidArgument, Unauthenticated and PermissionDenied. The final arm Ok(Ok(Err(status))) logs 'transport outcome is ambiguous', publishes RUN_DISPATCH_DEGRADED and sends agent_dispatch_unavailable_event (retryable true). execution-core prepare_resume and enforce_resume return failed_precondition('continuation_already_consumed' | 'continue_disabled' | ...). s7c-v3 section E says 'With NotSpent every arm is the committed one, byte for byte'. No committed test pins FailedPrecondition as degraded (grep of sse.rs found none), so changing it breaks nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Ask the lead for an explicit ruling. Either (a) scope the binding to the pre-consumed path in writing and record that the switch-off path keeps agent_dispatch_unavailable for refused segments, or (b) classify the closed refusal tokens for NotSpent too: a typed non-degraded frame with no RUN_DISPATCH_DEGRADED, keeping the committed terminalization behaviour. Whichever is chosen, the SPA contract must say which regime applies.

findings.issue: As specified the unit does not compile. spawn_consume_then_launch is bounded 'C: ApprovalConsumer + Send + static' and its spawned async block runs consume_then_launch(&consumer, ..).await. The future therefore holds &C across an await, and tokio::spawn needs that future to be Send, which requires C: Sync. The bound is missing. The same applies to the fake consumers in the race and drop tests.
findings.evidence: Design interface text: 'spawn_consume_then_launch<C: ApprovalConsumer + Send + static, T: Send + static>(C, ..)', 'async move block that runs consume_then_launch(&consumer, request, launch).await'. The committed ApprovedPlanSource pattern passes its source by reference and relies on a Sync source (GrpcApprovedPlanSource holds shared references).
findings.suggested_fix: Require C: ApprovalConsumer + Send + Sync + 'static, or move the consumer into an Arc, or take it by value in consume_then_launch. Make the fake consumers Sync and say so in the A4 step.

findings.file: apps/Model Plane/docs (switch runbook), deploy/docker-compose.yml, durable_loop_contract switch_table (S7c-B2)
findings.issue: The D1 coupled-flip consequences omit a plausible mismatch: parser skew between the switches that must flip together. AGENT_CONTINUE_AFTER_APPROVAL_ENABLED is parsed leniently (1, true, on, yes), but EXECUTION_EFFECT_LEDGER_ENABLED, EXECUTION_LOOP_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED, SESSION_CORE_LOOP_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED and the S7b resume switch are parsed strictly (the literal true). An operator who flips with 1, yes or on gets continue on and ledger off. That is mismatched flip A: the click is spent, then the executor refuses the replay. The failure matrix and the pins say nothing about it. The deploy order and coupled-flip text also never say the literal must be true.
findings.evidence: mp-contracts loop_fold.rs: continue_after_approval_from matches 1|true|on|yes; switch_from is strict 'true'. execution-core effect.rs ledger_enabled uses eq_ignore_ascii_case('true'). redteam-checklist INV-13 and the gaps list record this skew. The compose entries pass the raw value through.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the D1 consequences, the runbook paragraph and a failure-matrix row: all coupled switches must be set to the literal true. Add a contract pin (or a compose comment checked by a guard) that the ledger and resume parsers stay strict. Optionally note in the mismatch-A signature that 1 or yes on the ledger looks 'on' but is off.

findings.issue: Any ambiguous consume (10 s timeout, Unavailable, Internal and so on) ends in 503 with no launch. That strands a click that may already be committed, for the full 15 minute window. Launching anyway would be safe and strictly better. The executor's own consume wins if the gateway's did not commit, and is an allowed same-claim replay if it did (ledger on, the D1 rule). A concurrent other-token request is still refused at the executor with continuation_already_consumed before anything runs. The same holds for a connect-phase-only failure, where the request provably never left the gateway and a bounded redispatch is safe by construction. The timeout itself converts a slow-but-successful consume into a strand. D9 only fixes what a retry sees (409), so it does not forbid this.
findings.evidence: s7c-v3 section B: 'EVERY other code ... is the catch-all 503 continue_unavailable'; matrix row 'Pre-consume transport failure, timeout (10 s) or any other code'. prepare_resume (agent.rs) accepts consumed.consumed || (already_consumed && same_claim && ledger_enabled). The session-core replay branch hands the call to the claimant.
findings.suggested_fix: Either record this as a considered and rejected alternative with the reason (it weakens the 'only a won consume proceeds' invariant and the typed spent gating), or specify it: on an ambiguous consume still launch, mark the stream as maybe-spent, and keep 409 and 503 only for the definite codes. Failing that, drop the 10 s timeout, or make it much longer than the session-core statement timeout, so a slow success is not converted into a strand.

findings.file: s7c-v3 failure_matrix and apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/grpc.rs (run_agent admission checks)
findings.issue: The matrix has no row for executor admission-time refusals. Before prepare_resume consumes anything, run_agent can refuse for several reasons: bearer authentication (data-plane, inference, sandbox), authorize and authorize_run (a session-core call that can fail transiently), enforce_persistence_free_execution, enforce_run_context, enforce_resume and enforce_agent_route. In the committed flow all of these leave the approval unconsumed, so the user can try again. After a gateway pre-consume every one of them spends the click and strands the run until the renewed window ends. Only the switch case (mismatched flip B) is described. A transient authorize_run failure falls under the catch-all (Unavailable gives continue_outcome_unknown), but that is not stated, and the SPA contract and operator text present these as rare ledger or switch problems.

findings.issue: A new expiry race. The descriptor reaper deletes descriptors of every approval whose expires_at has passed, consumed or not. At HEAD the executor's consume reads the descriptor in the same transaction that wins the compare-and-set, so it is immune. After a gateway spend-only consume the executor reads the descriptor later, in the replay branch, in a different transaction. If expires_at falls between the two, the replay returns no call and the executor refuses approval_not_resumable. The click is spent and the run is stranded. The window is milliseconds and only near expiry, but it is new and not in the matrix.
findings.evidence: approval_delivery.rs: DELETE FROM approval_continuation_descriptors ... WHERE a.expires_at IS NOT NULL AND a.expires_at <= now(), with no consumed_at predicate. orchestration_store.rs replay branch: call = read_consumed_call(..) only when same_claim, and None when the row is gone.
findings.suggested_fix: Add AND a.consumed_at IS NULL to the reaper (the descriptor of a consumed approval is needed by its replay until the run ends), or list the race as an accepted residual in the failure matrix.

revised.summary:
v4 is the complete v3 design with three review findings applied. I re-verified each against committed source (the working tree is clean at HEAD 7a8e6cce; I read git show HEAD of sse.rs).

Finding 2 and 3 (same defect, both CONFIRMED): spawn_consume_then_launch could not compile. consume_then_launch takes &C and is awaited inside tokio::spawn; a held &C makes the future Send only if C: Sync, and the bound was Send only. Fix: trait ApprovalConsumer: Send + Sync (supertraits, so every bound C: ApprovalConsumer + 'static carries them), GrpcApprovalConsumer holds a tonic client clone and an Arc<str> bearer (both Send + Sync), the fakes in the tests are Sync, and a compile-time assertion in A4 proves the REAL consumer satisfies the spawn bounds. Also verified and now stated: agentic_run_stream is a plain fn that takes AppState and every bearer by value (not async, no borrows), so the launch closure is 'static by moving owned values into it, and T = Sse<ReceiverStream<..>> is Send.

Finding 1 (CONFIRMED, high): the binding text 'a refused or replayed segment is a confirmed rejection, never a degraded dispatch' was met only for a pre-consumed continuation. At HEAD is_confirmed_agent_dispatch_rejection matches only InvalidArgument, Unauthenticated, PermissionDenied; the executor's refusals (continue_disabled, continuation_already_consumed, approval_snapshot_mismatch, continue_in_progress and the rest) are FailedPrecondition or Aborted, so on the switch-off path they fall to the final arm, which publishes RUN_DISPATCH_DEGRADED and sends agent_dispatch_unavailable with retryable true. Ruling applied (a conservative reading that keeps both the binding and the earlier 'never terminalize a continuation the gateway did not need to' finding): the binding is read as two halves. (i) The three codes the committed code already treats as a confirmed rejection (InvalidArgument, Unauthenticated, PermissionDenied: resume_incomplete, resume_forbidden, auth failures) keep the committed confirmed-rejection arm, terminalization and agent_dispatch_rejected, for a NotSpent continuation, unchanged. (ii) A closed refusal that arrives as FailedPrecondition, Aborted or NotFound (and a zdr trailer refusal on any other code) from a continuation, spent by the gateway or not, is classified as a typed refusal frame: retryable false, never agent_dispatch_unavailable, no RUN_DISPATCH_DEGRADED, and NO terminalization (the committed degraded arm did not terminalize either, and a continuation_already_consumed after the replayed released step can arrive while another segment still runs). For a NotSpent continuation that frame carries NO approval_spent field, because the gateway cannot know whether the executor spent the approval; the SPA contract gets a third regime for it (refused, approval state unknown: re-read the approval, never auto-retry). Unreachable and Unknown outcomes of a NotSpent continuation keep the committed arms. This is a behaviour change only on /continue (a route that already needs AGENT_CONTINUE_AFTER_APPROVAL_ENABLED) with the resume switch off, listed as exception (e) of the byte-identity statement; the lead should confirm the reading (open question), and if the lead prefers to scope the binding to the pre-consumed path, the change is deleting one arm and one test group.

B. PRE-CONSUME RULES AND THE DETACHED TASK
Pure map preconsume_refusal(Result<bool, tonic::Status>) -> Result<(), PreconsumeRefusal> where PreconsumeRefusal is Closed(StatusCode, &'static str) or Status(tonic::Status): Ok(true) proceeds; Ok(false) (already consumed, whatever the claim, the same token included) is 409 continuation_already_consumed; NotFound is 404 approval_not_found; FailedPrecondition with message approval_not_granted, approval_expired or approval_not_resumable is 409 with that code, any other FailedPrecondition 409 not_resumable; InvalidArgument is 400 continue_incomplete; PermissionDenied and Unauthenticated become Status(..) and the handler answers crate::http_routes::grpc_status_to_http (the same flat or typed ZDR body the owner check and the reads already return; this is the one documented place a session-core message text reaches the caller, it is closed session-core wording and never the claim token); EVERY other code (Unavailable, DeadlineExceeded, Internal, Unknown, Cancelled, Aborted, ResourceExhausted, Unimplemented, anything new) is the catch-all 503 continue_unavailable, ambiguous by definition because the consume may have committed. Logs carry the gRPC code and run_id only.
Detach (finding 2/3 applied). trait ApprovalConsumer: Send + Sync { fn consume(&self, ConsumeApprovalRequest) -> impl Future<Output = Result<bool, tonic::Status>> + Send }. The supertraits are required: consume_then_launch holds &C across an await inside tokio::spawn, which makes the future Send only if C: Sync. GrpcApprovalConsumer owns a clone of state.orchestration_client (a tonic client over a Channel: Send + Sync) and a clone of the session bearer (Arc<str>-backed: Send + Sync), so it satisfies both; every fake consumer in tests holds only Sync state (atomics, a Mutex, a tokio Notify; never a Cell or RefCell). consume builds the request with authenticated_session_request, wraps the RPC in tokio::time::timeout(PRECONSUME_TIMEOUT = 10 s, a constant, no new env) and maps Elapsed to Status::deadline_exceeded; it returns response.consumed and reads no other field. async fn consume_then_launch<C: ApprovalConsumer, T>(&C, request, launch: impl FnOnce() -> T) -> Result<T, PreconsumeRefusal> is the pure sequencing unit. fn spawn_consume_then_launch<C, T>(consumer: C, request, launch: impl FnOnce() -> T + Send + 'static) -> oneshot::Receiver<Result<T, PreconsumeRefusal>> with bounds C: ApprovalConsumer + 'static (Send + Sync come from the trait) and T: Send + 'static holds the ONLY tokio::spawn of the path: it creates the oneshot, spawns an async move block that owns the consumer and runs consume_then_launch(&consumer, request, launch).await and sends the outcome (a closed receiver is ignored), and returns the receiver. Result<T, PreconsumeRefusal> is Send because tonic::Status and StatusCode are. In continue_run T is Sse<ReceiverStream<Result<Event, Infallible>>>, which is Send. The launch closure must own everything (state, run, bearers moved in; the consumer and request built from clones BEFORE the closure moves model_bearer). A compile-time proof in A4: a test fn that instantiates spawn_consume_then_launch with GrpcApprovalConsumer and with the concrete T, so a regression of any bound fails to build. A client disconnect drops the receiver, never the task, so a won consume is always followed by the launch; the stream task's sends are already ignored on a closed channel. continue_run: switch off, Ok(launch()); switch on, match spawn_consume_then_launch(..).await { Ok(Ok(sse)) => Ok(sse), Ok(Err(Closed(s, c))) => continue_error(s, c), Ok(Err(Status(st))) => grpc_status_to_http(&st), Err(_) => continue_error(503, continue_unavailable) }. Residual window, honest: a gateway process crash, a timeout that fires after the server committed, or a rolling restart between the consume and the RunAgent send leaves a spent click and a non-terminal run until the renewed deadline ends; /continue streams are not registered in the drain registry today (pre-existing), so the detached task is not either (follow-up).

Inside agentic_run_stream compute `let continuing = resume.is_some();` before resume is moved.
Pure classify_continue_dispatch_failure(&tonic::Status) -> ContinueDispatchFailure { Refused(&'static str), Unreachable, Unknown }. Order: (1) if mp_contracts::zdr_refusal::Refusal::from_status(&status) is Some, Refused("durable_mutation_forbidden") when its code is the durable-mutation one, else Refused("continue_refused") (never the message); (2) NotFound is Refused("approval_not_found"); (3) FailedPrecondition, Aborted, InvalidArgument, PermissionDenied or Unauthenticated with a message exactly in CONTINUE_EXECUTOR_MESSAGE_TOKENS is Refused(that token), any other message there is Refused("continue_refused") (never echoed); (4) dispatch_never_reached_execution_core(&status) is Unreachable; (5) everything else (other Unavailable, DeadlineExceeded, Internal, Cancelled, the follow deadline, a join error) is Unknown.
continue_refusal_event(request_id, run_id, token, spend) -> Event is ChatEvent::Error { code: token, message: token with spaces, retryable: false } with run_id added to the payload and, ONLY for SpentByGateway, approval_spent: true (the pattern agent_dispatch_unavailable_event uses). continue_failure_event(request_id, run_id, &ContinueDispatchFailure) -> Event (spent regime only): Refused(t) -> continue_refusal_event(.., t, SpentByGateway); Unreachable sends continue_unreachable; Unknown sends continue_outcome_unknown, all retryable false, run_id and approval_spent true; a local RunAgent request-construction failure sends continue_refused. dispatch_unknown_event(spend, request_id, run_id) returns the old agent_dispatch_unavailable_event for NotSpent and continue_outcome_unknown for SpentByGateway; the three agent_dispatch_unavailable_event sites (deadline, join error, final ambiguous arm) call it.
Arm order for Ok(Ok(Err(status))) in agentic_run_stream, top to bottom:
 1. SPENT arm, guard spend.is_spent(): classify; Refused(t) sends continue_refusal_event(.., t, SpentByGateway) with no DEGRADED publish; Unreachable and Unknown publish RUN_DISPATCH_DEGRADED and send continue_failure_event. NEVER terminalizes (a spent continuation can be refused with continuation_already_consumed while another segment still runs; D9 leaves unreachable executors to the renewed window).
 2. committed confirmed-rejection arm (is_confirmed_agent_dispatch_rejection: InvalidArgument | Unauthenticated | PermissionDenied), UNCHANGED for NotSpent: terminalizes, agent_dispatch_rejected. This is the literal 'confirmed rejection' half of the binding (resume_incomplete, resume_forbidden, auth failures).
 3. NEW typed-refusal arm, guard continuing && !spend.is_spent() && matches!(classify(&status), Refused(_)): sends continue_refusal_event(.., token, NotSpent) (no approval_spent field, retryable false), publishes NO RUN_DISPATCH_DEGRADED, does NOT terminalize (the committed degraded arm it replaces did not terminalize either). This is the 'never a degraded dispatch' half: a refused or replayed segment (FailedPrecondition continuation_already_consumed, continue_disabled, approval_snapshot_mismatch, not_releasable, continue_in_progress, resume_checkpoint_unavailable, authority_*, NotFound, a zdr trailer refusal on another code) is never reported as agent_dispatch_unavailable. The frame deliberately says nothing about whether the approval is spent (the executor may have consumed before refusing); it means 'the executor refused; re-read the approval before any retry; do not retry automatically'.
 4. committed dispatch_never_reached_execution_core arm (terminalizes as Unreachable), unchanged for NotSpent.
 5. committed final ambiguous arm (DEGRADED, dispatch_unknown_event(NotSpent) = agent_dispatch_unavailable, retryable true), unchanged for NotSpent; reached by NotSpent continuations only for Unreachable-not-connect and Unknown classes.
The Err(error) request-construction branch gets an early spent path before its terminalization. Logs add the closed token and run_id; never the claim token, the approval content or an upstream message.
What a pre-consumed continuation leaves behind: run non-terminal, approval spent, obligation renewed at the consume, so session-core recovery terminalizes it 15 minutes after the consume if nothing heartbeats. Post-response frames (agent_run_failed, agent_run_state_unknown, agent_run_output_unavailable, subscription failures) keep their committed retryable values; the connected frame's approval_spent true is what tells the client not to re-POST.
connected_payload(run_id, thread_id, request_id, spend) -> Value is a tiny extraction of the inline json!; for NotSpent it is byte-identical to the committed payload; for SpentByGateway it adds approval_spent: true.

F. CLIENT-VISIBLE VOCABULARIES (closed, test-pinned, gateway-owned)
HTTP, CONTINUE_HTTP_REFUSALS (10): continue_disabled 409, not_resumable 409, continue_incomplete 400, missing_bearer 401, approval_not_found 404, approval_not_granted 409, approval_expired 409, approval_not_resumable 409, continuation_already_consumed 409, continue_unavailable 503. The BFF relays 8 (all but continue_incomplete, which its own guard preempts, and missing_bearer, which maps to unauthorized). Other statuses (owner check, reads, ZDR typed refusals, a consume PermissionDenied or Unauthenticated) keep grpc_status_to_http's body, and every such HTTP error happens before any consume, so it says not spent. Any HTTP response that is not 200 is not spent except continuation_already_consumed (spent, by this client earlier or by another click) and continue_unavailable (unknown).
Stream, CONTINUE_FRAME_REFUSALS (22) in three groups. Message tokens carried by the executor (CONTINUE_EXECUTOR_MESSAGE_TOKENS, 17): continue_disabled, resume_incomplete, continuation_already_consumed, approval_not_granted, approval_expired, approval_not_resumable, approval_action_mismatch, approval_snapshot_mismatch, not_releasable, authority_widened, authority_space_mismatch, authority_route_mismatch, continue_space_scope_unsupported, continue_in_progress, resume_checkpoint_unavailable, not_resumable, resume_forbidden. Code-derived (2): approval_not_found (NotFound), durable_mutation_forbidden (zdr trailer). Gateway-made (3): continue_refused, continue_unreachable, continue_outcome_unknown. Three REGIMES for a frame (the SPA contract and the descriptor text say so): (1) approval_spent true (any frame of a pre-consumed continuation, including connected): spent, retryable false, follow the run, never re-POST. The gateway sends "loop" only with its switch on and RunDetail.resumable. The executor downgrades "loop" to stage 1 when its own resume, checkpoint or ledger switch is off, or for a ZDR or waived run: a downgrade, never a refusal. segment_no is 0 and ignored; step_id, tool_name, action_fingerprint and brief are empty. There is NO new AgentResume field: consumed_by_gateway is dropped (D1), field 9 stays reserved, field 10 stays unused.
2. The replay rule (D1), identical in both stages, independent of the executor's resume switch: the executor's own ConsumeApproval proceeds when consumed.consumed || (consumed.already_consumed && consumed.same_claim && effect::ledger_enabled()); otherwise FailedPrecondition continuation_already_consumed. S7b moves this rule verbatim into consume_for_resume and must neither add an attestation nor accept a replay with the ledger off. After a gateway pre-consume EVERY executor consume is such a replay (consumed false, already_consumed true, same_claim true, the descriptor returned to the claimant).
3. Closed refusal tokens the executor may return after the consume, as gRPC code plus exact message: FailedPrecondition continuation_already_consumed | approval_not_resumable | approval_snapshot_mismatch | not_releasable | authority_widened | authority_space_mismatch | authority_route_mismatch | continue_space_scope_unsupported | resume_checkpoint_unavailable | not_resumable (run ended, from the claim) | continue_disabled | approval_not_granted | approval_expired | approval_action_mismatch; Aborted continue_in_progress; InvalidArgument resume_incomplete; PermissionDenied resume_forbidden (claim Space revocation); a ZDR trailer refusal (zdr_refusal kind zdr_durable_mutation_forbidden; the gateway keys on the trailer, not the message); NotFound (session-core text) for an approval or run that vanished. Anything else reaches the client as continue_refused: safe and unhelpful; a new token needs a row in CONTINUE_EXECUTOR_MESSAGE_TOKENS and the guard in B2. A claim failure after a won consume is a fallback to stage 1, not a refusal (D3, fold not closed), except the fatal ones above. S7b must keep using FailedPrecondition or Aborted for refusals it wants shown as typed refusals: InvalidArgument, Unauthenticated and PermissionDenied from RunAgent take the gateway's committed confirmed-rejection arm and TERMINALIZE the run on a switch-off continuation.
4. Every refusal returns from run_agent_with_route BEFORE heartbeat_managed_agent_run, finalize or any terminal write and leaves the run non-terminal and the managed obligation untouched. continuation_already_consumed from the replayed released step (after phase 2) is the one refusal that may arrive while another segment still runs; the gateway relies on this and never terminalizes a continuation on a FailedPrecondition or Aborted refusal.
5. Content-free closed log lines at the executor as live-proof evidence: resume_stage (in_place | stage_one) and fallback_reason (the RestoreFailure token) on one line per continuation, plus REQUESTED of S7b: one warn line resume_replay_refused with reason=ledger_off and run_id when the replay rule refuses, so a mismatched flip is recognisable from the executor side too.

7. D6 as a deploy precondition: the release action s{N}.tool_1_approved is reserved through the ledger whatever its effect class in both stages (S7b step 6) before the gateway switch flips.
8. S7b may rely on the managed obligation having been renewed to now + 15 minutes at the gateway's spend-only consume, so no recovery lease can fire between the gateway consume and the executor heartbeat. The executor stopping when HeartbeatManagedRunResponse.already_terminal is true is a recorded follow-up (D7).

invariants: The gateway consumes an approval at most once per /continue: only after every refusal check, only for a persistent turn, only with EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED on; only a won consume (consumed == true) proceeds; every other answer, the same claim token included, is 409 continuation_already_consumed (or a closed refusal).

Consume and launch are one detached task owned by spawn_consume_then_launch (the only tokio::spawn of the path): a client disconnect cannot spend an approval without RunAgent being sent. Test- and source-guarded. The consumer trait is Send + Sync and the launch closure owns everything it uses (compile-time test).

A won spend-only consume renews the run's managed obligation deadline in the same transaction (state open, deadline now + MANAGED_DEADLINE_SECS, lease cleared, only open and processing states, scoped by run_id and org_id); a replay, a lost race or a full consume never renews; a database error rolls the consume back.

The gateway never holds a consumed call's content: omit_call is set, session-core does not read, decrypt or return it, one boolean is read, and logs carry the gRPC code, a closed token and run_id only, never the claim token, call content or an upstream message.

The only place an upstream message text can reach a caller from the consume path is grpc_status_to_http for PermissionDenied and Unauthenticated, the same body the owner check and the reads return; every other consume failure is a closed code.

The typed spent arms (approval_spent true) are gated on the gateway's own local knowledge that it pre-consumed (ApprovalSpend::SpentByGateway, set only inside the launch closure that runs after consumed == true), never on resume.is_some() and never on any executor field; no frame ever carries approval_spent true unless the gateway itself consumed the approval.

A continuation (spent or not) whose RunAgent is refused with FailedPrecondition, Aborted or NotFound (or a zdr trailer refusal on another code) is never reported as agent_dispatch_unavailable, never publishes RUN_DISPATCH_DEGRADED and is never terminalized by the gateway; its frame is retryable false and carries run_id; without a gateway pre-consume it carries NO approval_spent field. InvalidArgument, Unauthenticated and PermissionDenied from RunAgent for a continuation the gateway did not pre-consume keep the committed confirmed-rejection arm (terminalization, agent_dispatch_rejected).

The gateway never terminalizes a pre-consumed continuation; every pre-consumed failure frame is retryable false, carries run_id and approval_spent true, and is never agent_dispatch_*; the connected frame of a pre-consumed continuation carries approval_spent true, and for NotSpent it is byte-identical to the committed payload.

The mode the gateway sends is 'loop' only with the switch on and RunDetail.resumable, else 'segment'; no other value; segment_no 0; hint fields empty; there is NO attestation field; a wrong hint costs a stage-1 fallback and nothing else.
A continuation never reads, claims or injects the thread's approved plan or grant and states no rung, floor, Space, route or tools.

RunDetail.resumable stays readable by every reader of the run at RPC level (a boolean) and never reaches a browser (run_detail_value is an allowlist); park_reason stays owner-or-service; a pause fold whose approval is consumed is not resumable.

The BFF relays only a (code, status) pair from the closed list with its own fixed message; every other upstream error is model_error or unauthorized; SSE bytes are relayed untouched and the relay body still passes tests/sse_relay_no_allowlist.rs.

The executor, not the gateway, owns what a continuation runs: tools, authority, mode and the approved call come from the paused snapshot; the executor's consume replay is the only reader of the descriptor.

With EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED off, the RPC sequence to session-core's approval store and to execution-core and the RunAgent bytes of /continue are the committed ones, with the stated exceptions (a) to (e) of approach A, all confined to the /continue route.

One /continue route, one AgentResume literal (continue_resume), one segment_no literal, one ConsumeApprovalRequest literal in the gateway, one agentic_run_stream call in continue_run, one loop_resume_enabled() read in continue_run.

Coupled flip: the gateway resume switch is never on unless the executor's ledger and continue switches are on; all switches default off in compose; the resume switch is the same variable on gateway and executor.

Fixed: trait ApprovalConsumer: Send + Sync, spawn bound C: ApprovalConsumer + 'static (supertraits carry Send + Sync), GrpcApprovalConsumer built from Sync parts, Sync fakes in tests, a compile-time test instantiating the real consumer and the concrete Sse T, a durable_loop_contract guard with a drop-Sync mutation, and an A4 step that compiles continue_run_tests after each hunk. FINDING 1 (CONFIRMED in substance, high): at HEAD is_confirmed_agent_dispatch_rejection matches only InvalidArgument | Unauthenticated | PermissionDenied, and the final arm of agentic_run_stream publishes RUN_DISPATCH_DEGRADED and sends agent_dispatch_unavailable (retryable true); the executor's continuation refusals are FailedPrecondition or Aborted, so on the switch-off path v3 left a refused or replayed segment as a degraded dispatch while claiming byte identity. v3 flagged only the 'do not terminalize' half. Resolution: the binding is read in two halves (committed confirmed-rejection arm kept for the three codes; a typed non-degraded, non-terminalizing refusal frame for FailedPrecondition, Aborted, NotFound and zdr-trailer refusals on every continuation), approval_spent is claimed only by the gateway's own pre-consume, a third SPA regime and a chatRunContinueUnflaggedRefusalOf guard were added, byte identity gains exception (e), the failure matrix, invariants, tests, a (c2) contract guard with mutations, a handler-level scenario pair and live stage s7-H2 were added, and the ruling is put to the lead as an acknowledgement item with the alternatives ((a) scope to the pre-consumed path; (b) terminalize a closed subset). The earlier finding that the gateway must not terminalize a continuation another segment may still be running is preserved: the new arm does not terminalize.
